title.zh: 卷三百十六 列傳第七十五 包拯 吳奎 趙抃子:屼 唐介子:淑问 义问 孙:恕
title.en: Volume 316 Biographies 75: Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, Zhao Bian and Son: Wu, Tang Jie and Son: Shuwen, Yi Wen, Grandson: Shu
title.raw: 卷三百十六 列傳第七十五 包拯 吳奎 趙抃子:屼 唐介子:淑问 义问 孙:恕 Volume 316 Biographies 75: Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, Zhao Bian and Son: Wu, Tang Jie and Son: Shuwen, Yi Wen, Grandson: Shu

sentences.zh: 包拯，字希仁，廬州合肥人也。

translations.literal: Bao Zheng, styled Xiren, was a man of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zheng, whose courtesy name was Xiren, came from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 始舉進士，除大理評事，出知建昌縣。

translations.literal: At first he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed as an examiner in the Court of Judicial Review, and went out as magistrate of Jianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was made an examiner in the Court of Judicial Review and sent out to serve as magistrate of Jianchang County.

sentences.zh: 以父母皆老，辭不就。

translations.literal: Because both parents were old, he declined and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Both his parents were elderly, so he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 得監和州稅，父母又不欲行，拯即解官歸養。

translations.literal: He obtained supervision of the Hezhou tax office, but his parents again did not wish him to go, so Zheng immediately resigned his office and returned home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a post supervising the tax office at Hezhou, but his parents again did not want him to leave, so Zheng at once resigned and went home to care for them.

sentences.zh: 後數年，親繼亡，拯廬墓終喪，猶裴徊不忍去，里中父老數來勸勉。

translations.literal: Several years later his parents died in succession; Zheng lived in a hut by the graves through the full mourning period, still lingering and unwilling to leave, and the elders of the village came repeatedly to urge him on.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later his parents died one after another. Zheng kept vigil by their graves through the full mourning period, still lingering and unable to tear himself away, until the village elders came again and again to urge him on.

sentences.zh: 久之，赴調，知天長縣。

translations.literal: After a long while he reported for reassignment and was made magistrate of Tianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he reported for a new assignment and was appointed magistrate of Tianchang County.

sentences.zh: 有盜割人牛舌者，主來訴。

translations.literal: There was a thief who cut off someone's ox tongue; the owner came to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When someone stole and cut off another man's ox tongue, the owner came to bring suit.

sentences.zh: 拯曰：「第歸，殺而鬻之。」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Just go home, slaughter it, and sell the meat."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng told him, "Go home, slaughter the beast, and sell the meat."

sentences.zh: 尋復有來告私殺牛者，拯曰：「何為割牛舌而又告之？」

translations.literal: Soon someone else came to report a private slaughter of an ox. Zheng said, "Why did you cut off the ox's tongue and then come to report him?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone else came to report an illicit slaughter of an ox. Zheng said, "Why did you cut off the ox's tongue and then come here to accuse him?"

sentences.zh: 盜驚服。

translations.literal: The thief was startled and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was struck with fear and confessed.

sentences.zh: 徙知端州，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Duanzhou and promoted to Defender-in-attendance of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Duanzhou as prefect and promoted to Defender-in-attendance of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 端土產硯，前守緣貢，率取數十倍以遺權貴。

translations.literal: Duan's native product was inkstones; previous prefects used the tribute obligation as a pretext and generally took dozens of times the quota to give to powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Duanzhou was known for its inkstones, and previous prefects had used the tribute quota as a pretext to take many times the required amount and present them to powerful families.

sentences.zh: 拯命制者才足貢數，歲滿不持一硯歸。

translations.literal: Zheng ordered the makers to produce only enough to meet the tribute quota; when his term ended he did not take a single inkstone home.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng ordered the craftsmen to make only what the tribute required, and when his term ended he did not carry a single inkstone home.

sentences.zh: 尋拜監察御史裏行，改監察御史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed provisional investigating censor, then changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed provisional investigating censor and then investigating censor in full.

sentences.zh: 時張堯佐除節度、宣徽兩使，右司諫張擇行、唐介與拯共論之，語甚切。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yaozuo was appointed to the two posts of military commissioner and palace commissioner; Remonstrance Counselor Zhang Zexing, Tang Jie, and Zheng jointly remonstrated, their language very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yaozuo was given both the military governorship and the palace commissionership, and Remonstrance Counselors Zhang Zexing and Tang Jie joined Zheng in opposing the appointments in the sharpest terms.

sentences.zh: 又嘗建言曰：「國家歲賂契丹，非禦戎之策。

translations.literal: He also once memorialized, saying, "The state's annual payments to the Khitan are not a policy for defending against barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He also once submitted a memorial saying, "The state's yearly payments to the Khitan are no way to defend the realm.

sentences.zh: 宜練兵選將，務實邊備。」

translations.literal: One should train troops and select generals, and earnestly strengthen frontier defenses."
translations.idiomatic: We should train the army, choose capable generals, and earnestly strengthen the border defenses."

sentences.zh: 又請重門下封駁之制，及廢錮贓吏，選守宰，行考試補蔭弟子之法。

translations.literal: He also requested restoring the Chancellery's system of sealed review and rebuttal, abolishing blocked registers for corrupt officials, selecting prefects and magistrates, and implementing examinations for filling hereditary privilege positions.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Chancellery's power of sealed review and rebuttal be restored, that corrupt officials be barred from office, that prefects and magistrates be chosen carefully, and that examinations be required for hereditary privilege appointments.

sentences.zh: 當時諸道轉運加按察使，其奏劾官吏多摭細故，務苛察相高尚，吏不自安，拯於是請罷按察使。

translations.literal: At that time transport commissioners on the various circuits were additionally made surveillance commissioners; their impeachments of officials mostly seized on trifles, striving for harsh scrutiny to outdo one another, so officials were ill at ease, and Zheng therefore requested abolishing the surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the time transport commissioners on the circuits were also made surveillance commissioners, and their impeachments often seized on petty matters as officials competed in harsh scrutiny; clerks lived in constant anxiety, and Zheng therefore asked that the surveillance commissionership be abolished.

sentences.zh: 去使契丹，契丹令典客謂拯曰：「雄州新開便門，乃欲誘我叛人，以刺疆事耶？」

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, the Khitan chief of reception said to Zheng, "Xiongzhou newly opened a convenience gate—do you mean to lure our defectors to spy on frontier affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, their chief of reception said to Zheng, "Xiongzhou has just opened a side gate—are you trying to lure our defectors across so you can spy on border affairs?"

sentences.zh: 拯曰：「涿州亦嘗開門矣，刺疆事何必開便門哉？」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Zhuozhou also once opened a gate—if you wished to spy on frontier affairs, why would you need to open a convenience gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, "Zhuozhou opened a gate too—if you wanted to spy on border affairs, why would you need a side gate?"

sentences.zh: 其人遂無以對。

translations.literal: The man then had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The man had no answer.

sentences.zh: 曆三司戶部判官，出為京東轉運使，改尚書工部員外郎、直集賢院，徙陝西，又徙河北，入為三司戶部副使。

translations.literal: He served as judicial secretary in the Ministry of Revenue of the Three Departments, went out as transport commissioner for Jingdong, was changed to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Works and diarist in the Hall for Treasuring Worthies, transferred to Shaanxi and then Hebei, and entered the capital as Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a judicial secretary in the Ministry of Revenue of the Three Departments, then went out as transport commissioner for Jingdong, was made Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Works and a diarist in the Hall for Treasuring Worthies, transferred to Shaanxi and then Hebei, and finally returned to the capital as Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 秦隴斜穀務造船材木，率課取於民；

translations.literal: The Xiegu office on the Qin-Long circuit for shipbuilding timber habitually levied collections from the people;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiegu timber office on the Qin-Long circuit, which supplied shipbuilding materials, habitually levied the cost from the people;

sentences.zh: 又七州出賦河橋竹索，恒數十萬，拯皆奏罷之。

translations.literal: and seven prefectures also paid levies in bamboo rope for river bridges, constantly reaching hundreds of thousands—all of which Zheng memorialized to abolish.
translations.idiomatic: and seven prefectures were also assessed bamboo rope for river bridges, year after year in sums of hundreds of thousands. Zheng memorialized to abolish all of these levies.

sentences.zh: 契丹聚兵近塞，邊郡稍警，命拯往河北調發軍食。

translations.literal: The Khitan massed troops near the frontier; border prefectures were somewhat alarmed, and Zheng was ordered to Hebei to coordinate the dispatch of army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan massed troops near the border and frontier prefectures grew uneasy, Zheng was ordered to Hebei to coordinate the dispatch of army provisions.

sentences.zh: 拯曰：「漳河沃壤，人不得耕，刑、洺、趙三州民田萬五千頃，率用牧馬，請悉以賦民。」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "The fertile lands along the Zhang River—people cannot farm them; fifteen thousand qing of commoners' fields in the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Zhao are largely used for pasturing horses. I ask that all be assigned to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "The rich soil along the Zhang River lies untilled because the people are not allowed to farm it. Fifteen thousand qing of farmland in Xing, Ming, and Zhao are largely used to pasture horses. I ask that all of it be turned over to the people."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: His request was approved.

sentences.zh: 解州鹽法率病民，拯往經度之，請一切通商販。

translations.literal: The salt laws of Jiezhou habitually harmed the people; Zheng went to survey them and requested opening all salt to general commerce.
translations.idiomatic: The salt laws of Jiezhou habitually burdened the people, so Zheng went to reorganize them and asked that salt trade be fully opened to merchants.

sentences.zh: 除天章閣待制、知諫院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin academician-at-call in the Tianzhang Pavilion and chief of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician-at-call in the Tianzhang Pavilion and put in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 數論斥權幸大臣，請罷一切內除曲恩。

translations.literal: He repeatedly criticized powerful favored ministers and requested abolishing all irregular inner appointments and petty favors.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly denounced powerful favorites at court and asked that all irregular inner appointments and petty favors be abolished.

sentences.zh: 又列上唐魏鄭公三疏，願置之坐右，以為高抬貴手。

translations.literal: He also listed and submitted the three memorials of Wei Zheng of Tang, expressing the wish to place them at the emperor's right hand as standards to lift one's eyes toward.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted the three memorials of Wei Zheng of Tang and asked that they be kept always at the emperor's right hand as models for enlightened judgment.

sentences.zh: 又上言天子當明聽納，辨朋黨，惜人才，不主先入之說，凡七事；

translations.literal: He also submitted that the Son of Heaven should clearly heed remonstrance, distinguish factions, cherish talent, and not adhere to preconceived views—seven matters in all;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the Son of Heaven should listen openly to remonstrance, distinguish factions, cherish talent, and not cling to preconceived views—seven matters in all;

sentences.zh: 請去刻薄，抑僥倖，正刑明禁，戒興作，禁妖妄。

translations.literal: he requested removing harsh narrowness, curbing opportunistic advancement, rectifying punishments and clarifying prohibitions, warning against extravagant construction, and forbidding occult delusions.
translations.idiomatic: and he asked that harshness be removed, opportunism curbed, punishments rectified and prohibitions clarified, extravagant construction restrained, and occult delusions forbidden.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多施行之。

translations.literal: The court largely implemented these.
translations.idiomatic: The court put most of these into effect.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣直學士、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin academician in the Longtu Pavilion and overall transport commissioner for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin academician in the Longtu Pavilion and overall transport commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 嘗建議無事時徙兵內地，不報。

translations.literal: He had once proposed transferring troops to the interior in peacetime; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He had once proposed moving troops inland in peacetime, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 至是，請：「罷河北屯兵，分之河南兗、鄆、齊、濮、曹、濟諸郡，設有警，無後期之憂。

translations.literal: At this time he requested, "Abolish the stationed troops in Hebei and distribute them among the prefectures Yan, Yun, Qi, Pu, Cao, and Ji in Henan; if there is an alarm, there will be no worry about delayed reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Now he asked, "Disband the garrison troops in Hebei and distribute them among Yan, Yun, Qi, Pu, Cao, and Ji in Henan, so that if an alarm arises there will be no fear of reinforcements arriving too late.

sentences.zh: 借曰戍兵不可遽減，請訓練義勇，少給餱糧，每歲之費，不當屯兵一月之用，一州之賦，則所給者多矣。」

translations.literal: Even if one says frontier garrisons cannot be abruptly reduced, train militia volunteers and give them less dry rations—the annual cost would not equal one month's expense of stationed troops, and one prefecture's tax levy would supply more than enough."
translations.idiomatic: Even if frontier garrisons cannot be cut at once, train local militia and give them smaller rations: the yearly cost would be less than one month's upkeep for stationed troops, and a single prefecture's tax revenue would supply far more than enough."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 徙知瀛州，諸州以公錢貿易，積歲所負十余萬，悉奏除之。

translations.literal: He was transferred as prefect of Yingzhou; various prefectures using public funds for trade had accumulated debts of over one hundred thousand over the years—all of which he memorialized to cancel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yingzhou as prefect. Several prefectures had used public funds for trade and run up debts of more than one hundred thousand over the years; he memorialized to cancel them all.

sentences.zh: 以喪子乞便郡，知揚州，徙廬州，遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Because of his son's death he requested a convenient prefecture, was made prefect of Yangzhou, transferred to Luzhou, and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of his son he asked for a nearby prefecture, served as prefect of Yangzhou, was transferred to Luzhou, and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坐失保任，左授兵部員外郎、知池州。

translations.literal: Having failed in his guarantee responsibility, he was demoted to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of War and made prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had failed in a guarantee responsibility, he was demoted to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of War and made prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 復官，徙江寧府，召權知開封府，遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: His rank was restored; he moved to Jiangning Prefecture, was summoned to act as prefect of Kaifeng, and promoted to Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was restored, he was moved to Jiangning Prefecture, summoned to act as prefect of Kaifeng, and promoted to Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 拯立朝剛毅，貴戚宦官為之斂手，聞者皆憚之。

translations.literal: Zheng was stern and resolute at court; imperial kinsmen and eunuchs drew in their hands before him, and all who heard of him feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At court Zheng was stern and unyielding; even imperial kinsmen and eunuchs drew back before him, and all who heard his name feared him.

sentences.zh: 人以包拯笑比黃河清，童稚婦女，亦知其名，呼曰「包待制」。

translations.literal: People compared a smile from Bao Zheng to the Yellow River clearing; children and women too knew his name and called him "Commissioner Bao."
translations.idiomatic: People said that a smile from Bao Zheng was as rare as the Yellow River running clear; even children and women knew his name and called him "Commissioner Bao."

sentences.zh: 京師為之語曰：「關節不到，有閻羅包老。」

translations.literal: The capital had a saying about him: "If the bureaucratic seals do not reach you, there is still Old Lord Yama Bao."
translations.idiomatic: In the capital people said of him, "If the official seals never reach you, there is still Lord Yama Bao."

sentences.zh: 舊制，凡訟訴不得徑造庭下。

translations.literal: By old regulation, no litigant might go directly to the courthouse.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, litigants were not allowed to go straight to the courthouse.

sentences.zh: 拯開正門，使得至前陳曲直，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Zheng opened the main gate so people could come forward and state right and wrong; clerks did not dare deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng opened the main gate so that people could come before him and state their grievances, and the clerks no longer dared to deceive them.

sentences.zh: 中官勢族築園榭，侵惠民河，以故河塞不通，適京師大水，拯乃悉毀去。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and powerful families built gardens and pavilions encroaching on the Huimin Canal, so the canal was blocked; when the capital suffered a great flood, Zheng had all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and powerful families had built gardens and pavilions that encroached on the Huimin Canal and blocked its flow. When the capital was struck by a great flood, Zheng had all of these structures torn down.

sentences.zh: 或持地券自言有偽增步數者，皆審驗劾奏之。

translations.literal: Some held land deeds claiming false additions to measured areas—all were investigated, verified, and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone produced a land deed with a falsely inflated measurement, Zheng investigated, verified the fraud, and impeached the holder.

sentences.zh: 遷諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrance Counselor and acting Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Remonstrance Counselor and acting Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「東宮虛位日久，天下以為憂，陛下持久不決，何也？」

translations.literal: He memorialized, "The Eastern Palace has stood empty for a long time; the realm is anxious. Your Majesty delays decision—why?"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "The Eastern Palace has stood empty for a long time, and the realm is anxious. Why does Your Majesty delay so long in deciding?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「卿欲誰立？」

translations.literal: Renzong said, "Whom do you wish to establish?"
translations.idiomatic: Renzong said, "Whom do you wish to establish as heir?"

sentences.zh: 拯曰：「臣不才備位，乞豫建太子者，為宗廟萬世計也。

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Your servant, unworthy though I hold this post, asks to establish an heir early for the sake of the ancestral temples for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "I am unworthy of my post, but I ask that an heir be named early for the sake of the ancestral temples for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 陛下問臣欲誰立，是疑臣也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty asks whom I wish to establish, that is to doubt me.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty asks whom I wish to establish, that is to doubt my motives.

sentences.zh: 臣年七十，且無子，非邀福者。」

translations.literal: I am nearly seventy and have no son; I am not one who courts fortune."
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly seventy and have no son. I am not seeking personal advantage."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「徐當議之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "We shall discuss it in due course."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "We shall discuss it in due course."

sentences.zh: 請裁抑內侍，減節冗費，條責諸路監司，御史府得自舉屬官，減一歲休暇日，事皆施行。

translations.literal: He requested curbing inner attendants, reducing extraneous expenses, setting out regulations for circuit supervisors, allowing the Censorate to nominate its own subordinates, and cutting one year's holiday days—all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that inner attendants be restrained, wasteful spending reduced, circuit supervisors held to clear regulations, the Censorate allowed to nominate its own subordinates, and one year's holiday days cut from the calendar. All of these measures were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 張方平為三司使，坐買豪民產，拯劾奏罷之；

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping served as Commissioner of the Three Departments; on account of buying a powerful family's property, Zheng impeached and memorialized for his removal;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fangping served as Commissioner of the Three Departments, Zheng impeached him for buying property from a powerful family and had him removed from office;

sentences.zh: 而宋祁代方平，拯又論之；

translations.literal: when Song Qi replaced Fangping, Zheng remonstrated again;
translations.idiomatic: when Song Qi replaced Fangping, Zheng opposed him as well;

sentences.zh: 祁罷，而拯以樞密直學士權三司使。

translations.literal: Song Qi was removed, and Zheng as Hanlin academician in the Secretariat became acting Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi was removed, and Zheng, as Hanlin academician in the Secretariat, was made acting Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修言：「拯所謂牽牛蹊田而奪之牛，罰已重矣，又貪其富，不亦甚乎！」

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu said, "What Zheng has done is like leading an ox across another's field and then seizing the ox—the penalty was already heavy, yet he covets the wealth too—is that not excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu said, "Zheng is like the man who led his ox across another's field and then seized the ox as well: the punishment was already severe, yet he also covets the office's wealth—is that not going too far!"

sentences.zh: 拯因家居避命，久之乃出。

translations.literal: Zheng therefore stayed home to avoid the appointment; only after a long while did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng stayed at home to avoid the appointment and only after a long interval took up the post.

sentences.zh: 其在三司，凡諸管庫供上物，舊皆科率外郡，積以困民。

translations.literal: While at the Three Departments, all storehouses supplying court goods had customarily been levied from outer prefectures, accumulating hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the Three Departments, all storehouses that supplied goods to the court had customarily levied them from outer prefectures, a practice that had long burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 拯特為置場和市，民得無擾。

translations.literal: Zheng specially set up markets for purchase; the people were spared disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng set up dedicated purchasing markets so that the people were no longer harassed.

sentences.zh: 吏負錢帛多縲系，間輒逃去，並械其妻子者，類皆釋之。

translations.literal: Clerks owing money and silk were often bound; they would flee intermittently, and their wives and children would be shackled together with them—Zheng largely released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks who owed money or silk were often bound in chains; when they fled, their wives and children were shackled as well. Zheng released nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，為三司使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and made Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and made Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 數日，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: Within days he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Military Affairs Council.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Military Affairs Council.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷禮部侍郎，辭不受，尋以疾卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, declined and did not accept; soon he died of illness at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, but declined the appointment; not long after he died of illness at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡孝肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the temple name Xiaosu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Xiaosu.

sentences.zh: 拯性峭直，惡吏苛刻，務敦厚，雖甚嫉惡，而未嘗不推以忠恕也。

translations.literal: Zheng's nature was sternly upright; he hated harsh petty officials and strove for lenient sincerity; though he deeply detested evil, he never failed to apply loyalty and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was stern and upright by nature. He detested harsh petty officials and strove for generous fairness; though he hated wrongdoing fiercely, he always treated people with loyalty and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 與人不苟合，不偽辭色悅人，平居無私書，故人、親党皆絕之。

translations.literal: With others he did not compromise lightly, did not feign pleasant words to please people, had no private letters in ordinary times, and broke off ties with old friends and kin.
translations.idiomatic: He would not compromise lightly with others or put on a pleasant face to please them. In ordinary times he wrote no private letters, and he cut off contact even with old friends and relatives.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，衣服、器用、飲食如布衣時。

translations.literal: Though honored, his clothing, utensils, food, and drink were as in his commoner days.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose high, his clothing, utensils, food, and drink were no different from those of his days as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「後世子孫仕宦，有犯贓者，不得放歸本家，死不得葬大塋中。

translations.literal: He once said, "If descendants in office commit graft, they shall not be returned to the family home for burial; when dead they shall not be buried in the great clan grave.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "If any descendant in office commits graft, he shall not be returned to the family home, and when he dies he shall not be buried in the clan grave.

sentences.zh: 不從吾志，非吾子若孫也。」

translations.literal: Whoever does not follow my intent is not my son or grandson."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever does not follow my will is not my son or grandson."

sentences.zh: 初，有子名繶，娶崔氏，通判潭州，卒。

translations.literal: Earlier he had a son named Chan who married the Cui clan, served as vice prefect of Tanzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had had a son named Chan, who married a woman of the Cui clan, served as vice prefect of Tanzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 崔守死，不更嫁。

translations.literal: Cui upheld her husband's death and did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Cui observed her husband's death and did not remarry.

sentences.zh: 拯嘗出其媵，在父母家生子，崔密撫其母，使謹視之。

translations.literal: Zheng had once dismissed a concubine who bore a child at her parents' home; Cui secretly supported the mother and had her watch over the child carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had once dismissed a concubine, who bore a child at her parents' home. Cui secretly supported the mother and had her care for the child attentively.

sentences.zh: 繶死後，取媵子歸，名曰綖。

translations.literal: After Chan died, they brought the concubine's son home and named him Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chan died, they brought the concubine's son into the household and named him Yan.

sentences.zh: 有奏議十五卷。

translations.literal: He left fifteen juan of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He left fifteen juan of memorials.

sentences.zh: 吳奎，字長文，濰州北海人。

translations.literal: Wu Kui, styled Changwen, was a man of Beihai in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kui, whose courtesy name was Changwen, came from Beihai in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 性強記，於書無所不讀。

translations.literal: His nature was strongly retentive; there was no book he did not read.
translations.idiomatic: He had a powerful memory and read every kind of book.

sentences.zh: 舉《五經》，至大理丞，監京東排岸。

translations.literal: He passed the Five Classics examination, rose to Assistant Director in the Court of Judicial Review, and supervised the Jingdong embankment office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Five Classics examination, rose to Assistant Director in the Court of Judicial Review, and supervised the Jingdong embankment office.

sentences.zh: 慶曆宿衛之變，奎上疏曰：「涉春以來，連陰不解，《洪範》所謂'皇之不極，時則有下伐上'者。

translations.literal: During the Qingli crisis of the palace guards, Kui submitted, "Since spring began, overcast skies have not cleared—the Hongfan speaks of 'when the sovereign lacks the mean, there is subordination attacking superiors.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli mutiny of the palace guards, Kui submitted a memorial saying, "Since spring began the skies have remained overcast without clearing—the Hongfan speaks of a time when the sovereign lacks the mean and subordinates rise against their superiors.

sentences.zh: 今衛士之變，起於肘腋，流傳四方，驚駭群聽。

translations.literal: Now the guards' mutiny arose at the elbow and armpit, spread in all directions, and shocked everyone's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Now the guards' mutiny has arisen at the emperor's very side, spread in every direction, and shocked the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 聞皇城司官六人，其五已受責，獨楊懷敏尚留。

translations.literal: I hear that of six officials of the Imperial City office, five have already been punished, but only Yang Huaimin remains.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that of the six officials of the Imperial City Bureau, five have already been punished, yet Yang Huaimin alone remains in office.

sentences.zh: 人謂陛下私近幸而屈公法，且獲賊之際，傳令勿殺，而左右輒屠之。

translations.literal: People say Your Majesty favored intimates and bent public law; moreover, when the culprits were captured, an order was issued not to kill, yet those at your side promptly slaughtered them.
translations.idiomatic: People say that Your Majesty has favored intimates and bent the law, and that when the culprits were captured an order was issued not to kill them, yet those at your side promptly slaughtered them anyway.

sentences.zh: 此必其黨欲以滅口，不然，何以不奉詔？」

translations.literal: This must be their faction wishing to silence witnesses—otherwise why would they disobey the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: This must be their faction trying to silence witnesses. Otherwise why would they disobey the edict?"

sentences.zh: 遂乞召對面論，仁宗深器之。

translations.literal: He then requested a private audience to speak face to face, and Renzong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for a private audience to speak face to face, and Renzong came to value him highly.

sentences.zh: 再遷殿中丞，策賢良方正入等，擢太常博士、通判陳州。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Defender-in-attendance, entered the grade in the Examinations for Worthy and Incorrupt, and was elevated to Erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Defender-in-attendance, entered the top grade in the Examinations for Worthy and Incorrupt, and was elevated to Erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為右司諫，改起居舍人，同知諫院。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Remonstrance Counselor in the Bureau of Military Affairs, was changed to Recorder of the Left, and Associate Chief of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Remonstrance Counselor in the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Recorder of the Left, and Associate Chief of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 每進言，惟勸帝禁束左右奸幸。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke at court, he only urged the emperor to restrain wicked favorites at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke at court, he urged the emperor only to restrain the wicked favorites around him.

sentences.zh: 內東門闌得賂遺物，下吏研治，而開封用內降釋之。

translations.literal: At the inner east gate the guards seized bribed goods; subordinates investigated, but Kaifeng used an inner edict to release them.
translations.idiomatic: At the inner east gate the guards seized goods offered as bribes. Subordinates investigated the case, but Kaifeng used an inner edict to release the offenders.

sentences.zh: 奎劾尹魏瓘，出瓘越州。

translations.literal: Kui impeached the prefect Wei Guan and had Guan sent out to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kui impeached the prefect Wei Guan and had him sent out to Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 彭思永論事，詔詰所從受。

translations.literal: When Peng Siyong discussed affairs, an edict demanded where he had received his information.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Siyong spoke on state affairs, an edict demanded to know from whom he had received his information.

sentences.zh: 奎言：「御史法許風聞，若窮核主名，則後誰敢來告以事？

translations.literal: Kui said, "The censor's law permits hearsay; if one exhaustively traces the informant's name, then who afterward would dare report matters?
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "The law allows censors to act on hearsay. If every informant must be traced to the source, who afterward will dare to report wrongdoing?

sentences.zh: 是自塗其耳目也。」

translations.literal: That would be to block one's own ears and eyes."
translations.idiomatic: That would be to stop up one's own ears and eyes."

sentences.zh: 上為罷不問。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore dropped the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore dropped the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 郭承祐、張堯佐為宣徽使，奎連疏其不當，承祐罷使，出堯佐河中。

translations.literal: Guo Chengyou and Zhang Yaozuo were made palace commissioners; Kui submitted successive memorials that this was improper—Chengyou was removed from his commission and Yaozuo sent out to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chengyou and Zhang Yaozuo were made palace commissioners, Kui submitted successive memorials that the appointments were improper. Chengyou was removed from his commission and Yaozuo was sent out to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，頗多災異，奎極言其徵曰：「今冬令反燠，春候反寒，太陽虧明，五星失度，水旱作沴，饑饉薦臻，此天道之不順也。

translations.literal: During Huangyou there were many omens and anomalies; Kui spoke at length of their signs, saying, "Now winter's season runs warm in reverse, spring's season runs cold in reverse, the sun's light is diminished, the five planets lose their proper measure, flood and drought produce calamity, and famine comes repeatedly—this is Heaven's way not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era there were many portents and disasters, and Kui spoke at length of what they signified: "Winter has turned unseasonably warm, spring unseasonably cold, the sun's light has dimmed, the five planets have lost their proper courses, floods and droughts have brought calamity, and famine has come again and again. This is Heaven's way out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 自東徂西，地震為患，大河橫流，堆阜或出，此地道之不順也。

translations.literal: From east to west, earthquakes are a scourge, the great river flows across, mounds sometimes rise up—this is Earth's way not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: From east to west earthquakes have struck, the Yellow River has burst its banks, and mounds of earth have risen from the ground. This is the earth's way out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 邪曲害政，陰柔蔽明，群小紛爭，眾情壅塞，西、北貳敵，求欲無厭，此人事之不和也。

translations.literal: The crooked harm government, yin softness obscures clarity, petty men contend in confusion, the people's feelings are blocked, western and northern enemies are disloyal and their desires know no end—this is human affairs not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The crooked harm government, soft influences obscure clear judgment, petty men quarrel among themselves, the people's will is stifled, and enemies on the western and northern frontiers grow restless and insatiable. This is human affairs out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王之美，莫大於進賢退不肖。

translations.literal: Of an emperor's excellence, nothing is greater than advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the virtues of an emperor, none is greater than promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 今天下皆謂之賢，陛下知之而不能進；

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven call someone worthy, and Your Majesty knows it yet cannot advance him;
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone under Heaven calls certain men worthy, yet Your Majesty, though you know it, cannot promote them;

sentences.zh: 天下皆謂之不肖，陛下知之而不能退。

translations.literal: all under Heaven call someone unworthy, and Your Majesty knows it yet cannot remove him.
translations.idiomatic: and everyone calls certain men unworthy, yet Your Majesty, though you know it, cannot remove them.

sentences.zh: 內寵驕恣，近習回撓，陰盛如此，寧不致大異乎？

translations.literal: Inner favorites are arrogant and unrestrained, intimates bend affairs aside, yin influence is so strong—can this fail to bring great anomalies?
translations.idiomatic: Inner favorites grow arrogant and unrestrained, and those close at hand twist affairs to their will. With yin influence so strong, how can great portents fail to follow?

sentences.zh: 又十數年來下令及所行事，或有名而無實，或始是而終非，或橫議所移，或奸謀所破，故群臣百姓，多不甚信，以謂陛下言之雖切而不能行，行之雖銳而不能久。

translations.literal: Moreover, over the past dozen years your orders and actions have sometimes had name but no substance, sometimes begun right and ended wrong, sometimes been shifted by arbitrary debate, sometimes broken by wicked plots—so ministers and commoners largely do not trust them, saying that though Your Majesty speaks urgently you cannot carry it out, and though you carry it out sharply you cannot sustain it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for more than ten years your edicts and actions have sometimes been all name and no substance, sometimes right at the start and wrong at the end, sometimes overturned by reckless debate, sometimes undone by wicked plots. Ministers and commoners alike largely no longer trust them, saying that though Your Majesty speaks with urgency you cannot follow through, and though you follow through with vigor you cannot sustain it.

sentences.zh: 臣願謹守前詔，堅如金石，或敢私撓，必加之罪，毋為人所測度，而取輕於天下。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that you strictly keep former edicts, firm as metal and stone; if anyone dares privately obstruct them, punishment must be imposed; do not let people gauge you and thereby be held lightly by all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty strictly uphold your former edicts, firm as metal and stone. If anyone dares privately obstruct them, let punishment follow. Do not let others read your intentions and thereby hold you lightly in the eyes of the realm."

sentences.zh: 唐介論文彥博，指奎為黨，出知密州。

translations.literal: Tang Jie criticized Wen Yanbo and identified Kui as a partisan; Kui was sent out as prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Jie criticized Wen Yanbo he named Kui as a partisan, and Kui was sent out to serve as prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 加直集賢院，徙兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He was added as diarist in the Hall for Treasuring Worthies and transferred as transport commissioner for the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a diarist in the Hall for Treasuring Worthies and transferred to serve as transport commissioner for the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 入判登聞檢院、同修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He entered to judge the Petition Office, jointly compiled the imperial diary, and drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital to judge the Petition Office, helped compile the imperial diary, and was put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，會其主加稱號，要入賀。

translations.literal: On an embassy to the Khitan, it happened that their ruler added a title and demanded that one enter to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, their ruler had just taken a new title and demanded that the Song envoy enter to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 奎以使事有職，不為往。

translations.literal: Kui, having duties pertaining to the embassy, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, citing his duties as envoy, refused to go.

sentences.zh: 歸遇契丹使于塗，契丹以金冠為重，紗冠次之。

translations.literal: On the return journey he met a Khitan envoy on the road; the Khitan regarded the gold cap as weighty and the gauze cap as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he met a Khitan envoy on the road. The Khitan regarded the gold cap as the more honored garment and the gauze cap as secondary.

sentences.zh: 故事，使者相見，其衣服重輕必相當。

translations.literal: By precedent, when envoys met, the weight of their garments had to match.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when envoys met, the rank shown by their dress had to be equivalent.

sentences.zh: 至是，使者服紗冠，而要奎盛服。

translations.literal: On this occasion the envoy wore a gauze cap but demanded that Kui wear full ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the Khitan envoy wore a gauze cap but demanded that Kui appear in full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 奎殺其儀以見，坐是出知壽州。

translations.literal: Kui reduced the ceremony to meet him and for this was sent out as prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kui reduced the ceremony with which he met the envoy, and for this was sent out to serve as prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 至和三年，大水，詔中外言得失。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhihe, great floods occurred, and an edict called on court and realm to speak of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhihe era there was a great flood, and an edict called on officials inside and outside the court to speak frankly about what had gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 奎上疏曰：「陛下在位三十四年，而儲嗣未立。

translations.literal: Kui submitted a memorial, saying, "Your Majesty has reigned thirty-four years, yet the heir has not been established.
translations.idiomatic: Kui submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty has reigned for thirty-four years, yet no heir has been established.

sentences.zh: 在禮，大宗無嗣，則擇支子之賢者。

translations.literal: In ritual, when the main line has no heir, one selects a worthy son of a collateral branch.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, when the main line has no heir, one chooses a worthy son from a collateral branch.

sentences.zh: 以昭穆言，則太祖、太宗之曾孫，所宜建立，以系四海之望。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of ancestral order, a great-grandson of Taizu or Taizong is the one who should be established, to bind the hopes of all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: In terms of the ancestral line, a great-grandson of Taizu or Taizong should be established to satisfy the hopes of all within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 俟有皇子則退之，而優其禮於宗室，誰曰不然？

translations.literal: When a prince is born he may be set aside, yet honor his standing among the imperial clan—who would say otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: If a son is later born to Your Majesty, the heir may step aside, yet still be honored among the imperial clan. Who could object to that?

sentences.zh: 陛下勿聽奸人邪謀，以誤大事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not listen to wicked men's evil plots and thereby err in a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not listen to the wicked plots of evil men and thereby miss this great matter.

sentences.zh: 若倉卒之際，柄有所歸，書之史冊，為萬世歎憤。

translations.literal: If in a sudden crisis power falls to someone, and it is written in the historical records, it will be a source of lament and anger for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If in a sudden crisis power falls into the wrong hands and that is written in the historical records, it will be a source of lament and outrage for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 臣不願以聖明之資，當危亡之比。

translations.literal: Your servant does not wish that with sage brilliance you should face a time comparable to peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to see Your Majesty's sage brilliance tested at a moment comparable to national peril.

sentences.zh: 此事不宜優遊，願蚤裁定。

translations.literal: This matter should not be treated leisurely; I wish you would decide it early.
translations.idiomatic: This matter brooks no delay. I beg Your Majesty to decide it soon.

sentences.zh: 定之不速，致宗祀無本，鬱結群望，推之咎罰，無大於此。」

translations.literal: If it is not decided swiftly, causing the ancestral sacrifices to lack a root and the hopes of the multitude to be pent up, then pushing blame and punishment, nothing is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: If it is not decided quickly, the ancestral sacrifices will lack their foundation and the people's hopes will remain pent up. Of all faults that invite blame and punishment, none is greater than this."

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，拜翰林學士，權開封府。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by his words and appointed him Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by his words and appointed him Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 奎達于從政，應事敏捷，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Kui was accomplished in administration, quick in handling affairs, and clerks did not dare deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was skilled in government, quick in handling affairs, and the clerks did not dare deceive him.

sentences.zh: 富人孫氏辜榷財利，負其息者，至評取物產及婦女。

translations.literal: The wealthy Sun clan monopolized profits; those who owed their interest were even made to yield property and women by appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy Sun clan had monopolized profits, and those who owed them interest were even forced to surrender property and women in settlement.

sentences.zh: 奎發孫宿惡，徙其兄弟于淮、閩，豪猾畏斂。

translations.literal: Kui exposed the Sun clan's long-standing evil and moved their brothers to Huai and Min; powerful schemers feared and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kui exposed the Sun clan's long-standing crimes and moved their brothers to Huai and Min. The powerful and unscrupulous were cowed into restraint.

sentences.zh: 居三月，治聲赫然。

translations.literal: Within three months his reputation for good governance was conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months his reputation for good governance was widely known.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士、知成都府，以親辭，改鄆州，復還翰林，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Chengdu; citing his parents he declined, was changed to Yanzhou, returned again to the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Military Affairs Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Chengdu, but declined on account of his parents and was instead made prefect of Yanzhou. He later returned to the Hanlin Academy and was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Military Affairs Council.

sentences.zh: 治平中，丁父憂，居喪毀瘠，廬於墓側，歲時潔嚴祭祀，不為浮屠事。

translations.literal: During Zhiping he mourned his father, was emaciated in mourning, lived in a hut beside the grave, at the seasons performed pure and solemn sacrifices, and did not engage in Buddhist affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he mourned his father, grew gaunt with grief, and lived in a hut beside the grave. At the proper seasons he performed solemn sacrifices and would have nothing to do with Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 神宗初立，奎適終制，以故職還朝。

translations.literal: When Shenzong first ascended, Kui had just completed mourning and returned to court in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong first ascended the throne, Kui had just completed his mourning period and returned to court in his former post.

sentences.zh: 逾月，參知政事。

translations.literal: After a month he became Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 時已召王安石，辭不至，帝顧輔臣曰：「安石曆先帝朝，召不赴，頗以為不恭。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi had already been summoned but declined to come; the emperor looked at his assisting ministers and said, "Anshi served through the former emperor's reign and when summoned did not come—I consider that rather disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had already been summoned but had not come. The emperor turned to his ministers and said, "Anshi served through my father's reign. When summoned he did not come, and I consider that rather disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 今又不至，果病耶，有所要耶？

translations.literal: Now again he does not come—is he truly ill, or does he want something?
translations.idiomatic: Now again he has not come. Is he truly ill, or is he asking for something?

sentences.zh: 曾公亮曰：「安石文學器業，不敢為欺。」

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang said, "Anshi's literary learning and capacity—I would not dare deceive you about them."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang said, "In literary learning and capacity Anshi is not to be deceived about."

sentences.zh: 奎曰：「臣嘗與安石同領群牧，見其護短自用，所為迂闊。

translations.literal: Kui said, "Your servant once served with Anshi jointly overseeing the herds and saw that he shields his faults and acts on his own; what he does is impractical and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "I once served with Anshi in overseeing the herds and saw that he covers his faults and insists on his own way. His conduct is impractical and unrealistic.

sentences.zh: 萬一用之，必紊亂綱紀。」

translations.literal: If by any chance he is used, he will surely disorder the laws and standards."
translations.idiomatic: If he is ever put in power, he will surely throw the laws and institutions into disorder."

sentences.zh: 乃命知江寧。

translations.literal: Anshi was therefore ordered to Jiangning as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was therefore appointed prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 奎嘗進言：「陛下在推誠應天，天意無他，合人心而已。

translations.literal: Kui once advanced the view, "Your Majesty should respond to Heaven by extending sincerity; Heaven's intent is nothing else but to align with the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Kui once said to the emperor, "Your Majesty should respond to Heaven by extending sincerity. Heaven's intent is nothing other than to align with the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 若以至誠格物，物莫不以至誠應，則和氣之感，自然而致。

translations.literal: If with utmost sincerity you reach things, nothing will fail to respond with utmost sincerity, and the response of harmonious qi will come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you reach all things with utmost sincerity, all things will respond with utmost sincerity, and the harmony of qi will come of itself.

sentences.zh: 今民力困極，國用窘乏，必俟順成，乃可及他事。

translations.literal: Now the people's strength is exhausted to the limit and state revenues are strained; one must wait until things proceed smoothly before other matters can be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people's strength is exhausted and state revenues are strained. Other matters must wait until the realm is once again in good order.

sentences.zh: 帝王所職，惟在於判正邪，使君子常居要近，小人不得以害之，則自治矣。」

translations.literal: An emperor's duty lies solely in judging right and wrong, keeping gentlemen constantly in important posts near at hand, and not letting petty men harm them—then governance will right itself."
translations.idiomatic: An emperor's duty lies solely in distinguishing right from wrong, keeping gentlemen in important posts close at hand, and not letting petty men harm them. Then the state will govern itself."

sentences.zh: 帝因言：「堯時，四凶猶在朝。」

translations.literal: The emperor then said, "In Yao's time the Four Evils were still at court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "In Yao's time the Four Evils were still at court."

sentences.zh: 奎曰：「四凶雖在，不能惑堯之聰明。

translations.literal: Kui said, "Though the Four Evils were present, they could not confuse Yao's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Though the Four Evils were present, they could not confuse Yao's clarity.

sentences.zh: 聖人以天下為度，未有顯過，固宜包容，但不可使居要近地爾。」

translations.literal: A sage takes all under Heaven as his measure; if there is no conspicuous fault, tolerance is proper, but one must not let such men occupy important posts near at hand."
translations.idiomatic: A sage measures all under Heaven broadly. If men have no conspicuous fault, they may be tolerated, but they must not be allowed to hold important posts close at hand."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王陶，以論文德不押班事詆韓琦，奎狀其過。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wang Tao, in discussing Wende's failure to join the procession, slandered Han Qi; Kui memorialized his faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-chief Wang Tao attacked Han Qi over the matter of Wende's failure to join the procession, Kui memorialized Tao's own faults.

sentences.zh: 詔除陶翰林學士，奎執不可。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tao Hanlin academician; Kui held firm that this could not be.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Tao Hanlin academician, but Kui firmly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 陶又疏奎阿附。

translations.literal: Tao again memorialized that Kui was partisan and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: Tao in turn memorialized that Kui was partisan and fawning.

sentences.zh: 陶既出，奎亦以資政殿大學士知青州。

translations.literal: After Tao was sent out, Kui also became Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao was sent out, Kui too was made Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 司馬光諫曰：「奎名望清重，今為陶絀奎，恐大臣皆不自安，各求引去。

translations.literal: Sima Guang remonstrated, "Kui's reputation is pure and weighty; now because of Tao, Kui is demoted—I fear the great ministers will all be ill at ease and each seek to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remonstrated, "Kui's reputation is pure and weighty. To demote him because of Tao may leave the great ministers ill at ease and each seeking to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，于四方觀聽非宜。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended; for the regard of the four quarters this is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just ascended the throne. This is not how the realm should see you."

sentences.zh: 帝乃召奎歸中書。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Kui back to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Kui back to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及琦罷相，竟出知青州。

translations.literal: When Qi left the chancellorship, Kui was ultimately sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi left the chancellorship, Kui was ultimately sent out to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，年五十八。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，諡曰文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of War, with the posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of War, with the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 奎喜獎廉善，有所知輒言之，言之不從，不止也。

translations.literal: Kui delighted in encouraging integrity and goodness; whenever he knew of someone he would speak of him, and if not followed he did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Kui delighted in encouraging integrity and goodness. Whenever he knew of someone worthy he would speak up, and if the court did not listen he would not stop.

sentences.zh: 少時甚貧，，既通貴，買田為義莊，以賙族党朋友。

translations.literal: In youth he was very poor; once he attained high rank he bought land for a charity estate to relieve clan, party, and friends.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was very poor. Once he rose high he bought land for a charity estate to support his clan, associates, and friends.

sentences.zh: 沒之日，家無餘資，諸子至無屋以居，當時稱之。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the family had no surplus wealth; his sons even had no house in which to live—at the time this was praised.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died his family had no surplus wealth, and his sons had not even a house to live in. People praised him for this at the time.

sentences.zh: 趙抃，字閱道，衢州西安人。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian, styled Yuedao, was a man of Xi'an in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian, whose courtesy name was Yuedao, came from Xi'an in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為武安軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating officer of the Wu'an military commission.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as investigating officer of the Wu'an military commission.

sentences.zh: 人有赦前偽造印，更赦而用者，法吏當以死。

translations.literal: A man had forged a seal before an amnesty and used it after a further amnesty; the legal officers sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: A man had forged a seal before an amnesty and used it after a further amnesty. The legal officers sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 抃曰：「赦前不用，赦後不造，不當死。」

translations.literal: Bian said, "Before the amnesty he did not use it; after the amnesty he did not forge—he should not die."
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "Before the amnesty he did not use the seal, and after the amnesty he did not forge it. He should not die."

sentences.zh: 讞而生之。

translations.literal: The sentence was revised and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was revised and the man was spared.

sentences.zh: 知崇安、海陵、江原三縣，通判泗州。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of the three counties Chong'an, Hailing, and Jiangyuan, and vice prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chong'an, Hailing, and Jiangyuan, and as vice prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 濠守給士卒廩賜不如法，聲欲變，守懼，日未入，輒閉門不出。

translations.literal: The prefect of Hao gave soldiers grain allowances contrary to regulation; rumor said they would mutiny; the prefect was afraid and, before the sun had set, would close the gates and not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Hao had issued soldiers' grain allowances contrary to regulation, and there were rumors of mutiny. The prefect was so afraid that before sunset each day he shut the gates and would not go out.

sentences.zh: 轉運使檄抃攝治之，抃至，從容如平時，州以無事。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner ordered Bian to act in his place and govern; Bian arrived and was as composed as in ordinary times, and the prefecture was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner ordered Bian to take charge. When Bian arrived he was as composed as ever, and the prefecture remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士曾公亮未之識，薦為殿中侍御史，彈劾不避權幸，聲稱凜然，京師目為「鐵面御史。」

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Zeng Gongliang did not know him and recommended him as Attending Censor; in impeachments he did not avoid the powerful and favored; his reputation was stern, and the capital called him the "Iron-faced Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Zeng Gongliang, who did not know him, recommended him as Attending Censor. In his impeachments he did not spare the powerful and favored, his reputation was formidable, and the capital called him the "Iron-faced Censor."

sentences.zh: 其言務欲朝廷別白君子小人，以謂：「小人雖小過，當力遏而絕之；

translations.literal: His words strove to have the court distinguish gentlemen from petty men, saying, "Though petty men commit small faults, one should vigorously restrain and cut them off;
translations.idiomatic: He urged the court to distinguish clearly between gentlemen and petty men, saying, "Even small faults by petty men should be vigorously checked and cut off;

sentences.zh: 君子不幸詿誤，當保全愛惜，以成就其德。」

translations.literal: if gentlemen unfortunately err, one should preserve and cherish them to complete their virtue."
translations.idiomatic: but if gentlemen unfortunately err, they should be preserved and cherished so that their virtue may be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 溫成皇后之喪，劉沆以參知政事監護，及為相，領事如初。

translations.literal: At the mourning for Empress Wencheng, Liu Hang as Vice Grand Councillor supervised the rites; when he became chancellor he continued to direct affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the mourning for Empress Wencheng, Liu Hang as Vice Grand Councillor supervised the rites. When he became chancellor he continued to direct the funeral affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 抃論其當罷，以全國體。

translations.literal: Bian argued that he should withdraw to preserve the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bian argued that he should withdraw from those duties to preserve the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 又言宰相陳執中不學無術，且多過失；

translations.literal: He also said that Chancellor Chen Zhizhong was unlearned and without skill, and moreover had many faults;
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Chancellor Chen Zhizhong was unlearned and incompetent and had committed many faults;

sentences.zh: 宣徽使王拱辰平生所為及奉使不法；

translations.literal: that Palace Commissioner Wang Gongchen's conduct through life and on embassy were unlawful;
translations.idiomatic: that Palace Commissioner Wang Gongchen's conduct throughout his life and on embassy had been unlawful;

sentences.zh: 樞密使王德用、翰林學士李淑不稱職；

translations.literal: that Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Deyong and Hanlin academician Li Shu were unfit for their posts;
translations.idiomatic: and that Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Deyong and Hanlin academician Li Shu were unfit for their posts;

sentences.zh: 皆罷去。

translations.literal: all were removed.
translations.idiomatic: all were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 吳充、鞠真卿、刁約以治禮院吏，馬遵、呂景初、吳中復以論梁適，相繼被逐。

translations.literal: Wu Chong, Ju Zhenqing, and Diao Yue for disciplining the Rites Academy clerks, and Ma Zun, Lü Jingchu, and Wu Zhongfu for criticizing Liang Shi, were successively driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong, Ju Zhenqing, and Diao Yue had been driven out for disciplining clerks of the Rites Academy, and Ma Zun, Lü Jingchu, and Wu Zhongfu for criticizing Liang Shi.

sentences.zh: 抃言其故，悉召還。

translations.literal: Bian spoke of the reasons and all were summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Bian explained why they had been punished, and all were summoned back.

sentences.zh: 呂溱、蔡襄、吳奎、韓絳既出守，歐陽修、賈黯復求郡。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, Cai Xiang, Wu Kui, and Han Jiang had already gone out as prefects; Ouyang Xiu and Jia An again sought prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, Cai Xiang, Wu Kui, and Han Jiang had already been sent out as prefects, and Ouyang Xiu and Jia An were again asking for prefectural posts.

sentences.zh: 抃言：「近日正人端士紛紛引去，侍從之賢如修輩無幾，今皆欲去者，以正色立朝，不能諂事權要，傷之者眾耳。」

translations.literal: Bian said, "Recently upright gentlemen have one after another withdrawn; worthy attendants like Xiu are few, and now all wish to leave because they stand at court with proper color and cannot flatter powerful figures—those who wound them are many."
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "Recently upright gentlemen have been withdrawing one after another. Worthy attendants like Xiu are few, and now they too wish to leave because they stand at court with integrity and will not flatter the powerful. Many have been wounded by this."

sentences.zh: 修、黯由是得留，一時名臣，賴以安焉。

translations.literal: Xiu and An thereby were able to remain; eminent ministers of the time relied on this for stability.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and An were thereby able to remain at court, and the famous ministers of the age owed their stability to Bian.

sentences.zh: 請知睦州，移梓州路轉運使，改益州。

translations.literal: He requested to know Muzhou, was moved as transport commissioner for the Zizhou circuit, and was changed to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to serve as prefect of Muzhou, was made transport commissioner for the Zizhou circuit, and was then transferred to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀地遠民弱，吏肆為不法，州郡公相饋餉。

translations.literal: Shu territory was remote and the people weak; officials wantonly acted unlawfully, and prefectures and districts publicly exchanged gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was remote and its people weak. Officials acted lawlessly, and prefectures and districts openly exchanged gifts among themselves.

sentences.zh: 抃以身帥之，蜀風為變。

translations.literal: Bian took the lead in person and Shu customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian led by personal example, and the customs of Shu were transformed.

sentences.zh: 窮城小邑，民或生而不識使者，抃行部無不至，父老喜相慰，奸吏竦服。

translations.literal: In remote towns and small districts the people might live their lives without knowing an envoy; Bian on inspection tours went everywhere; elders gladly comforted one another, and wicked officials were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: In remote towns and small districts some people lived their whole lives without ever seeing an inspector. Bian on his tours went everywhere. The elders rejoiced to greet one another, and corrupt officials were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 召為右司諫。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Remonstrance Counselor in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Remonstrance Counselor in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 內侍鄧保信引退兵董吉燒煉禁中，抃引文成、五利、鄭注為比，力論之。

translations.literal: Inner attendant Deng Baoxin had a retired soldier Dong Ji conduct alchemical firing in the palace; Bian cited Wencheng, Wuli, and Zheng Zhu as comparisons and argued forcefully against it.
translations.idiomatic: When inner attendant Deng Baoxin had a retired soldier named Dong Ji conduct alchemical firing within the palace, Bian cited Wencheng, Wuli, and Zheng Zhu as precedents and argued forcefully against it.

sentences.zh: 陳升之副樞密，抃與唐介、呂海、范師道言升之奸邪，交結宦，進不以道。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; Bian with Tang Jie, Lü Hai, and Fan Shidao said Shengzhi was wicked and depraved, fraternized with eunuchs, and advanced by improper means.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shengzhi was made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, Bian joined Tang Jie, Lü Hai, and Fan Shidao in saying that Shengzhi was wicked and depraved, fraternized with eunuchs, and had advanced by improper means.

sentences.zh: 章二十餘上，升之去位。

translations.literal: More than twenty memorials were submitted, and Shengzhi left his post.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty memorials were submitted, and Shengzhi was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 抃與言者亦罷，出知虔州。

translations.literal: Bian and those who spoke with him were also dismissed; he went out as prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and those who had spoken with him were also dismissed, and Bian was sent out as prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 虔素難治，抃禦之嚴而不苛，召戒諸縣令，使人自為治。

translations.literal: Qian had always been hard to govern; Bian controlled it strictly but not harshly, summoned and admonished the county magistrates, and had people govern themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou had always been hard to govern. Bian ruled it strictly but not harshly, summoned the county magistrates to admonish them, and let the people govern themselves.

sentences.zh: 令皆喜，爭盡力，獄以屢空。

translations.literal: The magistrates were all pleased and strove with one another to do their utmost; the prisons were repeatedly empty.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates were all pleased and strove to do their best, and the prisons were repeatedly empty.

sentences.zh: 嶺外仕者死，多無以為歸，抃造舟百艘，移告諸郡曰：「仕宦之家，有不能歸者，皆於我乎出。」

translations.literal: Officials beyond the ranges who died often had no means to return home; Bian built a hundred boats and sent notice to the various prefectures, saying, "Official families that cannot return—all shall depart from me."
translations.idiomatic: Officials who died beyond the ranges often had no means to return home. Bian built a hundred boats and sent notice to the various prefectures saying, "If any official family cannot return home, let them all depart from me."

sentences.zh: 於是至者相繼，悉授以舟，並給其道裏費。

translations.literal: Thereupon arrivals came in succession; all were given boats and also provided travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they came in succession, and he gave them all boats and also provided their travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 召為侍御史知雜事，改度支副使，進天章閣待制、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs, changed to Vice Commissioner of Revenue, and advanced to Hanlin academician-at-call in the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs, made Vice Commissioner of Revenue, and promoted to Hanlin academician-at-call in the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時賈昌朝以故相守魏，抃將按視府庫，昌朝使來告曰：「前此，監司未有按視吾藏者，恐事無比，若何？

translations.literal: At that time Jia Changchao was defending Wei as a former grand councilor. Bian was about to inspect the prefectural treasury. Changchao sent a messenger to report, saying, "Until now no circuit supervisor has ever inspected our stores. I fear there is no precedent for this—what shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jia Changchao was serving as military prefect of Wei on account of his former rank. Bian was about to inspect the prefectural treasury. Changchao sent a messenger to say, "Until now no circuit supervisor has ever inspected our stores. I fear there is no precedent for this—what shall we do?

sentences.zh: 抃曰：「舍是，則他郡不服。」

translations.literal: Bian said, "If I omit this, then other prefectures will not be convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Bian said, "If I skip this, the other prefectures will not accept it."

sentences.zh: 竟往焉。

translations.literal: In the end he went.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he went anyway.

sentences.zh: 昌朝不悅。

translations.literal: Changchao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao was displeased.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔募義勇，過期不能辦，官吏當坐者八百餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, there was an edict to recruit local volunteers. When the deadline passed the quota still could not be met, and more than eight hundred officials were liable for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered the recruitment of local volunteers. When the deadline passed the quota still could not be filled, and more than eight hundred officials were liable for punishment.

sentences.zh: 抃被旨督之，奏言：「河朔頻歲豐，故應募者少，請寬其罪，以俟農隙。」

translations.literal: Bian received an order to supervise the matter and memorialized, saying, "The region north of the Yellow River has had successive years of abundance, so few have answered the call. I ask that their punishments be eased to await the agricultural slack season.
translations.idiomatic: Bian received an imperial order to oversee the matter and memorialized, saying, "North of the Yellow River has had good harvests year after year, so few men have volunteered. I ask that their punishments be eased until the farming season ends."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 坐者獲免，而募亦隨足。

translations.literal: Those liable for punishment were pardoned, and recruitment promptly reached the quota as well.
translations.idiomatic: Those who would have been punished were pardoned, and the recruitment quota was soon filled as well.

sentences.zh: 昌朝始愧服。

translations.literal: Only then did Changchao feel ashamed and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Changchao feel ashamed and submit.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士、知成都，以寬為治。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of academic expositor in the Hall of Dragon Designs and appointed prefect of Chengdu, governing with lenience.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academic expositor in the Hall of Dragon Designs and prefect of Chengdu, and he governed with lenience.

sentences.zh: 抃向使蜀日，有聚為妖祀者，治以峻法。

translations.literal: When Bian had previously served in Shu, those who gathered for illicit cult rites were punished under severe law.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian had previously served in Shu, those who gathered for illicit cult sacrifices were punished under severe law.

sentences.zh: 及是，復有此獄，皆謂不免。

translations.literal: By this time such a case arose again, and everyone said the offenders could not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When such a case arose again, everyone assumed the offenders could not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 抃察其亡他，曰：「是特酒食過耳。」

translations.literal: Bian investigated and found no other crime and said, "This is merely an excess of food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Bian looked into the matter and found nothing else amiss. He said, "This is merely an excess of food and drink."

sentences.zh: 刑首惡而釋余人，蜀民大悅。

translations.literal: He punished the chief wrongdoer and released the rest, and the people of Shu were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He punished the ringleaders and released the rest, and the people of Shu were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 會榮諲除轉運使，英宗諭諲曰：「趙抃為成都，中和之政也。」

translations.literal: When Rong Yi was appointed transport commissioner, Emperor Yingzong instructed Yi, saying, "Zhao Bian as prefect of Chengdu—that is balanced and harmonious government.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong Yi was appointed transport commissioner, Emperor Yingzong told him, "Zhao Bian's government in Chengdu is balanced and harmonious government."

sentences.zh: 神宗立，召知諫院。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Bian was summoned as director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Bian was summoned to head the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 故事，近臣還自成都者，將大用，必更省府，不為諫官。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a close minister returned from Chengdu and was to be put to great use, he had to pass through a provincial or central office first and not serve as a remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a close minister returned from Chengdu and was slated for high office, he had to pass through a provincial or central post first and not serve as a remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 大臣以為疑，帝曰：「吾賴其言耳，苟欲用之，無傷也。」

translations.literal: The great ministers regarded this as doubtful, but the emperor said, "I rely on his counsel. If I wish to employ him, there is no harm in it.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers thought this irregular, but the emperor said, "I rely on his counsel. If I wish to use him, there is no harm in it."

sentences.zh: 及謝，帝曰：「聞卿匹馬入蜀，以一琴一鶴自隨，為政簡易，亦稱是乎？」

translations.literal: When Bian paid his thanks, the emperor said, "I hear you entered Shu with a single horse, taking only a zither and a crane with you, and governed simply and easily—is that also fitting?
translations.idiomatic: When Bian paid his respects, the emperor said, "I hear you entered Shu alone on horseback, with only a zither and a crane for company, and governed simply and easily—is that also fitting?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 抃感顧知遇，朝政有未協者，必密啟聞，帝手詔褒答。

translations.literal: Grateful for the emperor's favor and trust, whenever he found court policy awry Bian would secretly report it, and the emperor would reply with autograph edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the emperor's favor and trust, Bian would secretly report whenever he found court policy awry, and the emperor would reply with autograph edicts of praise.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，抃屢斥其不便。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, Bian repeatedly criticized the inconveniences of his policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi held power, Bian repeatedly criticized the harm in his policies.

sentences.zh: 韓琦上疏極論青苗法，帝語執政，令罷之。

translations.literal: Han Qi submitted a memorial arguing forcefully against the Green Sprouts Law. The emperor spoke to the chief ministers and ordered its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi submitted a memorial arguing forcefully against the Green Sprouts Law. The emperor told the chief ministers to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 時安石家居求去，抃曰：「新法皆安石所建，不若俟其出。」

translations.literal: At that time Anshi was at home requesting dismissal. Bian said, "The new laws were all established by Anshi—it would be better to wait until he comes out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Anshi was at home asking to resign. Bian said, "Anshi built all the new laws—it would be better to wait until he returns to office."

sentences.zh: 既出，安石持之愈堅。

translations.literal: Once Anshi came out, he held to them all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Anshi returned, he held to them all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 抃大悔恨，即上言：「制置條例司建使者四十輩，騷動天下。

translations.literal: Bian was deeply remorseful and at once submitted a memorial saying, "The Fiscal Planning Commission has established forty classes of envoys, disturbing all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was deeply remorseful and at once submitted a memorial saying, "The Fiscal Planning Commission has established forty kinds of envoys, disturbing the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 安石強辯自用，詆天下公論以為流俗，違眾罔民，順非文過。

translations.literal: Anshi argues forcefully and acts on his own, slandering public opinion throughout the empire as vulgar custom, defying the multitude and deceiving the people, following what is wrong and glossing over his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi argues obstinately and acts on his own, dismissing public opinion throughout the empire as vulgar custom, defying the multitude and deceiving the people, following what is wrong and glossing over his faults.

sentences.zh: 近者台諫侍從，多以言不聽而去；

translations.literal: Recently censors, remonstrators, and attendant courtiers have mostly left because their words were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Recently censors, remonstrators, and attendant courtiers have mostly left office because their counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 司馬光除樞密，不肯拜。

translations.literal: Sima Guang was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs but refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs but refused to accept the post.

sentences.zh: 且事有輕重，體有大小。

translations.literal: Moreover, affairs have lighter and heavier import, and the structure of government has greater and lesser parts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, some affairs are light and others heavy, and some parts of government are small and others great.

sentences.zh: 財利於事為輕，而民心得失為重；

translations.literal: Wealth and profit in affairs are light, while gains and losses in popular sentiment are heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Financial gain is a light matter, but winning or losing the people's hearts is a heavy one.

sentences.zh: 青苗使者于體為小，而禁近耳目之臣用舍為大。

translations.literal: Green Sprouts envoys are a small matter in the structure of government, while the appointment and dismissal of close ministers who serve the emperor's eyes and ears is a great one.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts envoys are a small matter in the structure of government, but the appointment and dismissal of close ministers who serve the emperor's eyes and ears is a great one.

sentences.zh: 今去重而取輕，失大而得小，懼非宗廟社稷之福也。」
