translations.literal: Now to abandon the heavy and take the light, to lose the great and gain the small—I fear this is not a blessing for the ancestral temple and state altars.
translations.idiomatic: Now to abandon the heavy and take the light, to lose the great and gain the small—I fear this is no blessing to the ancestral temple and the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 奏入，懇乞去位，拜資政殿學士、知杭州，改青州，時京東旱蝗，青獨多麥，蝗來及境，遇風退飛，盡墮水死。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he earnestly begged to leave office. He was made academician of the Hall for Treasuring Governance and prefect of Hangzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou. At that time Jingdong suffered drought and locusts, but Qingzhou alone had abundant wheat. When the locusts reached its border, they met wind and retreated in flight, all falling into the water and dying.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he earnestly asked to leave office. He was made academician of the Hall for Treasuring Governance and prefect of Hangzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou. Jingdong was then suffering drought and locusts, but Qingzhou alone had abundant wheat. When the locusts reached its border, a wind blew them back; they all fell into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 成都以戍卒為憂，遂以大學士復知成都。

translations.literal: Chengdu was troubled by garrison soldiers, so he was again made prefect of Chengdu as grand academician.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu was troubled by its garrison soldiers, so he was again made grand academician and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 召見，勞之曰：「前此，未有自政府往者，能為朕行乎？」

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor comforted him, saying, "Until now none has gone from the government to there—can you go for Us?
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, the emperor encouraged him, saying, "Until now no one has gone from the central government to that post—can you go for me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下有言，即法也，奚例之問？」

translations.literal: He replied, "When Your Majesty speaks, that is law—why ask about precedent?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When Your Majesty speaks, that is law—why ask about precedent?"

sentences.zh: 因乞以便宜從事。

translations.literal: He therefore requested discretionary authority to act as needed.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked for discretionary authority to act as needed.

sentences.zh: 既至蜀，治益尚寬。

translations.literal: Once he reached Shu, his governance increasingly favored lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Shu, his government grew ever more lenient.

sentences.zh: 有卒長立堂下，呼諭之曰：「吾與汝年相若，吾以一身入蜀，為天子撫一方。

translations.literal: A company chief stood below the hall. Bian called and instructed him, saying, "You and I are about the same age. I entered Shu alone to soothe one region for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A company chief stood below the hall. Bian called him forward and said, "You and I are about the same age. I came into Shu alone to soothe one region for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 汝亦宜清謹畏戢以率眾，比戍還，得餘貲持歸，為室家計可也。」

translations.literal: You too should be pure, careful, and restrained in awe to lead the men. When your garrison term ends and you carry home what you have saved, you may plan for your household.
translations.idiomatic: You too should be pure, careful, and restrained in awe to lead the men. When your term of service ends and you carry home what you have saved, you can provide for your household."

sentences.zh: 人喜轉相告，莫敢為惡，蜀郡晏然。

translations.literal: The men gladly told one another, none dared to do evil, and Shu prefecture was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers gladly passed the word along, none dared to do wrong, and the prefecture was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 劍州民私作僧度牒，或以為謀逆告，抃不師畀獄吏，以意決之，悉從輕比。

translations.literal: Commoners in Jianzhou privately forged monk ordination certificates. Some reported this as plotting rebellion. Bian did not hand the cases over to prison clerks but decided them according to his own judgment, and all were punished leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners in Jianzhou had been forging monk ordination certificates, and some reported this as plotting rebellion. Bian did not hand the cases over to prison clerks but decided them himself, and all were punished leniently.

sentences.zh: 謗者謂其縱逆黨，朝廷取具獄閱之，皆與法合。

translations.literal: Slanderers said he had indulged rebels, but the court took the complete case records to review them, and all accorded with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers said he had indulged rebels, but the court reviewed the complete case records and found that all his judgments accorded with the law.

sentences.zh: 茂州夷剽境上，懼討乞降，乃縛奴將殺之，取血以受盟。

translations.literal: Yi tribesmen from Maozhou raided the border. Fearing a punitive campaign, they begged to surrender and bound slaves they meant to kill, intending to use their blood to seal the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tribesmen from Maozhou raided the border. Fearing a punitive expedition, they begged to surrender and bound slaves they meant to kill, intending to use their blood to seal the oath.

sentences.zh: 抃使易用牲，皆歡呼聽命。

translations.literal: Bian had them change to using sacrificial animals instead, and all cheered and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Bian had them use sacrificial animals instead, and all cheered and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 乞歸，越州。

translations.literal: He asked to retire and was appointed prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and was appointed prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 吳越大饑疫，死者過半。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue suffered great famine and plague, and more than half the people died.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu-Yue region suffered great famine and plague, and more than half the people died.

sentences.zh: 抃盡救荒之術，療病，埋死，而生者以全。

translations.literal: Bian employed every famine-relief technique, treated the sick, buried the dead, and thereby preserved the living.
translations.idiomatic: Bian used every famine-relief measure at his disposal, treated the sick, buried the dead, and thereby preserved the living.

sentences.zh: 下令修城，使得食其力。

translations.literal: He ordered the repair of the city walls so the people could eat by their labor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered repairs to the city walls so the people could earn their food by their labor.

sentences.zh: 復徙杭，以太子少保致仕，而官其子屼提舉兩浙常平以便養。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Hangzhou, retired as junior guardian of the heir apparent, and his son Wu was given the post of intendant of the Liang-Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries for convenient support.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Hangzhou, retired as junior guardian of the heir apparent, and his son Wu was given the post of intendant of the Liang-Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries so he could care for his father.

sentences.zh: 屼奉抃遍游諸名山，吳人以為榮。

translations.literal: Wu attended Bian as he toured all the famous mountains, and the people of Wu regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu accompanied Bian as he toured all the famous mountains, and the people of Wu took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 元豐七年，薨，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng he died, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少師，諡曰清獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of junior preceptor of the heir apparent, and his posthumous name was Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of junior preceptor of the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 抃長厚清修，人不見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Bian was generous, steadfast, and pure in conduct, and people never saw him pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was generous, steadfast, and pure in conduct, and no one ever saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 平生不治貲業，不畜聲伎，嫁兄弟之女十數、他孤女二十余人，施德煢貧，蓋不可勝數。

translations.literal: All his life he did not amass property or keep entertainers. He married off more than ten daughters of his brothers and more than twenty other orphaned girls, and his beneficence to the solitary and poor was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he amassed no property and kept no entertainers. He married off more than ten daughters of his brothers and more than twenty other orphaned girls, and the kindness he showed the friendless and poor was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 日所為事，入夜必衣冠露香以告於天，不可告，則不敢為也。

translations.literal: Each day's deeds—at night he always put on robes and cap, burned incense, and reported them to Heaven. What could not be reported, he dared not do.
translations.idiomatic: Each day's deeds—at night he always dressed properly, burned incense, and reported them to Heaven. What he could not report, he dared not do.

sentences.zh: 其為政，善因俗施設，猛寬不同，在虔與成都，尤為世所稱道。

translations.literal: In government he was skilled at adapting measures to local custom. Sternness and lenience differed from place to place, but at Qianzhou and Chengdu he was especially praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: In government he was skilled at adapting measures to local custom. Sternness and lenience differed from place to place, but at Qianzhou and Chengdu he was especially praised.

sentences.zh: 神宗每詔二郡守，必以抃為言。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Shenzong summoned the prefects of those two prefectures, he always spoke of Bian as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Shenzong summoned the prefects of those two prefectures, he always held up Bian as the model.

sentences.zh: 要之，以惠利為本。

translations.literal: In essence, he took popular benefit as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In essence, he took the people's benefit as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 晚學道有得，將終，與屼訣，詞氣不亂，安坐而沒。

translations.literal: Late in life he studied the Way and gained attainment. Nearing death he took leave of Wu, his words and tone unperturbed, and died sitting peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he studied the Way and gained attainment. As death approached he took leave of Wu without disorder in word or tone, and died sitting peacefully.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓琦嘗稱抃真世人標表，蓋以為不可及雲。

translations.literal: Grand councilor Han Qi once praised Bian as truly a model for the world and considered him beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilor Han Qi once called Bian a true model for the world and considered him beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 子 屼

translations.literal: Son: Wu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wu

sentences.zh: 屼字景仁。

translations.literal: Wu, styled Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, whose courtesy name was Jingren.

sentences.zh: 由蔭登第，通判江州，改溫州，代還，得見。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he passed the examinations, served as vice-prefect of Jiangzhou, was transferred to Wenzhou, and upon returning from replacement duty had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he passed the examinations, served as vice-prefect of Jiangzhou, was transferred to Wenzhou, and upon completing his tour of duty returned to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 時抃已謝事，神宗命為太僕丞，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: At that time Bian had already retired. Shenzong appointed Wu vice director of the Imperial Stud and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bian had already retired. Shenzong appointed Wu vice director of the Imperial Stud and then promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 以父老請外，提舉兩浙常平。

translations.literal: On account of his father's age he requested an outside post and was made intendant of the Liang-Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was elderly, he asked for an outside post and was made intendant of the Liang-Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，復為御史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he again served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era he again served as censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「治平以前，大臣不敢援置親党于要塗，子弟多處管庫，甚者不使應科舉，與寒士爭進。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "Before the Zhiping era, great ministers did not dare recommend and place their kin in important posts. Sons and younger brothers mostly served in storehouse posts, and in extreme cases were not allowed to take the civil examinations, competing for advancement with poor scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Before the Zhiping era, great ministers did not dare place their kin in important posts. Sons and younger brothers mostly served in storehouse jobs, and in extreme cases were not even allowed to take the civil examinations, competing for advancement with poor scholars.

sentences.zh: 自王安石柄國，持內舉不避親之說，始以子雱列侍從，由是循習為常。

translations.literal: Since Wang Anshi held the state, advancing the doctrine that one should recommend relatives without avoiding kin, he first placed his son Fang among attendant courtiers, and from this it became customary practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Anshi held power, advancing the doctrine that one should recommend relatives without avoiding kin, he first placed his son Fang among attendant courtiers, and from that it became customary practice.

sentences.zh: 資望淺者，或居事權繁重之地；

translations.literal: Those of shallow qualifications sometimes occupied posts of heavy authority.
translations.idiomatic: Men of shallow qualifications sometimes held posts of heavy authority.

sentences.zh: 無出身者，或預文字清切之職，今宜杜絕其源。」

translations.literal: Those without examination credentials sometimes participated in refined clerical posts close to the emperor. Now the source of this should be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Men without examination credentials sometimes held refined clerical posts close to the emperor. Now this source should be cut off."

sentences.zh: 又言：「台諫之臣，或稍遷其位，而陰奪言責；

translations.literal: He also said, "Censors and remonstrators may be slightly promoted in rank while secretly stripped of the duty to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Censors and remonstrators may be given a slight promotion in rank while secretly stripped of the duty to speak.

sentences.zh: 或略行其言，而退與善地；

translations.literal: Or their words may be partly carried out while they are demoted to comfortable posts.
translations.idiomatic: Or their words may be partly carried out while they are sent off to comfortable posts.

sentences.zh: 或兩全並立，苟從講解；

translations.literal: Or both sides may be accommodated by agreeable compromise.
translations.idiomatic: Or both sides may be accommodated through easy compromise.

sentences.zh: 或置而不問，外示包容。

translations.literal: Or matters may be set aside without inquiry, outwardly showing tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Or matters may be set aside without inquiry, outwardly showing tolerance.

sentences.zh: 使忠鯁之士，蒙羞難退，皆朝廷所宜深察也。」

translations.literal: Thus loyal and blunt men suffer shame yet find it hard to withdraw—all matters the court ought to examine deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Thus loyal and blunt men suffer shame yet find it hard to withdraw—all of this the court ought to examine deeply."

sentences.zh: 傅堯俞、王岩叟、梁燾、孫升以事去，屼言：「諸人才能學術，為世推稱；

translations.literal: When Fu Yaoyu, Wang Yansou, Liang Tao, and Sun Sheng left office over affairs, Wu said, "These men's talent and learning are praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yaoyu, Wang Yansou, Liang Tao, and Sun Sheng left office over affairs, Wu said, "These men's talent and learning are praised throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 忠言嘉謨，見於已試，宜悉召還朝。」

translations.literal: Their loyal counsel and excellent plans have been proven in trial. All should be summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Their loyal counsel and excellent plans have already been tested in office. All of them should be summoned back to court."

sentences.zh: 所言皆切時務。

translations.literal: What he spoke all closely addressed current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he said closely addressed the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 避執政親嫌，改都官員外郎，出提點京東刑獄。

translations.literal: To avoid affinity with those in power, he was changed to vice director in the Bureau of Review and sent out as intendant of criminal justice for Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid conflict with those in power through family ties, he was made vice director in the Bureau of Review and sent out as intendant of criminal justice for Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 元符中，曆鴻臚、太僕少卿。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfu era he successively served as vice minister of ceremonial and vice director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfu era he served successively as vice minister of ceremonial and vice director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 曾布知樞密院，將白為都承旨，蔡卞摭其救傅堯俞事，遂不用。

translations.literal: When Zeng Bu was commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he was about to recommend Wu for appointment as director of reception, but Cai Bian dredged up his defense of Fu Yaoyu, and Wu was therefore not employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Bu was commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he was about to recommend Wu for appointment as director of reception, but Cai Bian dredged up his defense of Fu Yaoyu, and Wu was therefore passed over.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 初，抃廬母墓三年，縣榜其裏曰「孝弟」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bian kept vigil at his mother's grave for three years, and the county posted his neighborhood with the title "Filial and Brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bian kept vigil at his mother's grave for three years, and the county posted his neighborhood with the title "Filial and Brotherly."

sentences.zh: 處士孫侔為作《孝子傳》。

translations.literal: The recluse Sun Mou wrote a Biography of the Filial Son for him.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Sun Mou wrote a Biography of the Filial Son for him.

sentences.zh: 及屼執父喪，而甘露降墓木。

translations.literal: When Wu observed mourning for his father, sweet dew descended on the trees at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu observed mourning for his father, sweet dew descended on the trees at the grave.

sentences.zh: 屼卒，子雲又以毀死，人稱其世孝。

translations.literal: When Wu died, his son Yun also died from grief in mourning, and people called their line filial across generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu died, his son Yun also died from grief in mourning, and people called their family filial across generations.

sentences.zh: 唐介，字子方，江陵人。

translations.literal: Tang Jie, styled Zifang, was a man of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jie, whose courtesy name was Zifang, came from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 父拱，卒漳州，州人知其貧，合錢以賻，介年尚幼，謝不取。

translations.literal: His father Gong died at Zhangzhou. The people of the prefecture, knowing their poverty, pooled money for funeral expenses, but Jie was still young and declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong died at Zhangzhou. The people of the prefecture, knowing how poor they were, pooled money for the funeral, but Jie was still young and declined to accept it.

sentences.zh: 擢第，為武陵尉，調平江令。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations, served as aide of Wuling, and was transferred as magistrate of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations, served as aide of Wuling, and was transferred to be magistrate of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 民李氏貲而吝，吏有求不厭，誣為殺人祭鬼。

translations.literal: A commoner surnamed Li was wealthy but stingy. An official whose requests were never satisfied falsely accused him of killing people to sacrifice to ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner surnamed Li was wealthy but stingy. An official whose demands were never satisfied falsely accused him of killing people to sacrifice to ghosts.

sentences.zh: 嶽守捕其家，無少長楚掠，不肯承。

translations.literal: The prefect of Yuezhou arrested his entire family. Without regard to age they were tortured, but they refused to confess.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Yuezhou arrested his entire family. Young and old alike were tortured, but they refused to confess.

sentences.zh: 更屬介訊之，無他驗。

translations.literal: The case was transferred to Jie to interrogate, and there was no other evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The case was transferred to Jie for interrogation, and he found no other evidence.

sentences.zh: 守怒白於朝，遣御史方偕徙獄別鞫之，其究與介同。

translations.literal: The prefect angrily reported to court. The censor Fang Xie was sent to transfer the prisoners and interrogate them separately, but the outcome was the same as Jie's.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect angrily reported to court. The censor Fang Xie was sent to transfer the prisoners and interrogate them separately, but he reached the same conclusion as Jie.

sentences.zh: 守以下得罪，偕受賞，介未嘗自言。

translations.literal: The prefect and those below were punished. Xie received a reward, but Jie never spoke of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and his subordinates were punished. Xie received a reward, but Jie never spoke of it himself.

sentences.zh: 知莫州任丘縣，當遼使往來道，驛吏以誅索破家為苦。

translations.literal: When he was magistrate of Renqiu in Mozhou, on the route traveled by Liao envoys, post station clerks suffered because exorbitant demands ruined families.
translations.idiomatic: When he was magistrate of Renqiu in Mozhou, on the route traveled by Liao envoys, post station clerks suffered because exorbitant demands ruined families.

sentences.zh: 介坐驛門，令曰：「非法所應給，一切勿與。

translations.literal: Jie sat at the post gate and ordered, "Whatever is not legally required to be supplied—supply none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sat at the post gate and ordered, "Whatever is not legally required to be supplied—supply none of it.

sentences.zh: 稍毀吾什器者，必執之。」

translations.literal: Whoever even slightly damages our implements must be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever even slightly damages our implements must be seized."

sentences.zh: 皆帖伏以去。

translations.literal: All submitted obediently and departed.
translations.idiomatic: All submitted obediently and departed.

sentences.zh: 沿邊塘水歲溢，害民田，中人楊懷敏主之，欲割邑西十一村地豬漲潦，介築提蘭之，民以為利。

translations.literal: In sum, along the border, pond waters overflowed every year and harmed the people's fields. The eunuch Yang Huaimin was in charge and wished to cut off land from eleven villages west of the county seat to hold back the floods. Jie built dikes and sluice gates, to the people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Along the border, pond waters overflowed every year and harmed the people's fields. The eunuch Yang Huaimin was in charge and wished to cut off land from eleven villages west of the county seat to hold back the floods. Jie built dikes and sluice gates, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 通判德州，轉運使崔嶧取庫絹配民而重其估。

translations.literal: Serving as vice-prefect of Dezhou, the transport commissioner Cui Yi took silks from the government storehouse to assign to the people and inflated the valuation.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Dezhou, the transport commissioner Cui Yi took silks from the government storehouse to assign to the people and inflated the valuation.

sentences.zh: 介留牒不下，且移安撫司責數之。

translations.literal: Jie kept the document and would not issue it, moreover shifted blame to the pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jie kept the document and would not issue it, and moreover shifted blame to the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 嶧怒，數馳檄按詰，介不為動。

translations.literal: Yi was furious and repeatedly sent urgent dispatches to investigate and question him; and Jie was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was furious and repeatedly sent urgent dispatches to investigate and question him; Jie was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 既而果不能行。

translations.literal: Before long afterward, it indeed could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it indeed could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史裏行，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In sum, he entered office as supernumerary investigating censor and was transferred to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as supernumerary investigating censor and was transferred to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 啟聖院造龍鳳車，內出珠玉為之飾。

translations.literal: In sum, at Qisheng Monastery they were building dragon-and-phoenix carriages, with pearls and jade from the inner treasury for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: At Qisheng Monastery they were building dragon-and-phoenix carriages, with pearls and jade from the inner treasury for ornament.

sentences.zh: 介言：「此太宗神禦所在，不可喧瀆；

translations.literal: Jie stated: "This is where Taizong's spirit tablet resides—it must not be profaned with noise;
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "This is where Taizong's spirit tablet resides—it must not be profaned with noise;

sentences.zh: 後宮奇靡之器，不宜過制。」

translations.literal: In sum, extravagant objects in the rear palaces should not exceed what regulations allow."
translations.idiomatic: extravagant objects in the rear palaces should not exceed what regulations allow."

sentences.zh: 詔亟毀去。

translations.literal: An imperial edict ordered them destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them destroyed at once.

sentences.zh: 張堯佐驟除宣徽、節度、景靈、群牧四使，介與包拯、吳奎等力爭之，又請中丞王舉正留百官班庭論，奪其二使。

translations.literal: Zhang Yaozuo was abruptly appointed to four posts—Xuanhui commissioner, military commissioner, Jingling commissioner, and director of the herds office. Jie, together with Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, and others, strove against it; and they also asked the vice censor-in-chief Wang Juzheng to detain the full corps of officials in the court to debate, and two of the appointments were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozuo was abruptly appointed to four posts—Xuanhui commissioner, military commissioner, Jingling commissioner, and director of the herds office. Jie, together with Bao Zheng, Wu Kui, and others, strove against it; they also asked the vice censor-in-chief Wang Juzheng to detain the full corps of officials in the court to debate, and two of the appointments were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 無何，復除宣徽使、知河陽。

translations.literal: Before long afterward, he was again appointed Xuanhui commissioner and prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed Xuanhui commissioner and prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 介謂同列曰：「是欲與宣徽，而假河陽為名耳，不可但已也。」

translations.literal: Jie stated to his colleagues: "This is intending to give him Xuanhui while using Heyang only as a pretext—it cannot simply be let go."
translations.idiomatic: Jie said to his colleagues: "This is intending to give him Xuanhui while using Heyang only as a pretext—it cannot simply be let go."

sentences.zh: 而同列依違，介獨抗言之。

translations.literal: His colleagues wavered; and Jie alone resisted and spoke out.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues wavered; Jie alone resisted and spoke out.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂曰：「除擬本出中書。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "The appointment draft originally came from the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong said: "The appointment draft originally came from the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 介遂劾宰相文彥博守蜀日造間金奇錦，緣閹侍通宮掖，以得執政；

translations.literal: Jie then impeached the Chief Councillor Wen Yanbo, saying that while Yanbo governed Shu he had woven gold brocades and sent them through eunuch attendants into the inner palace to gain power;
translations.idiomatic: Jie then impeached the chief minister Wen Yanbo, saying that while Yanbo governed Shu he had woven gold brocades and sent them through eunuch attendants into the inner palace to gain power;

sentences.zh: 今顯用堯佐，益自固結，請罷之而相富弼。

translations.literal: now that Yaozuo was openly employed, Yanbo further strengthened his ties—Jie asked that Yanbo be removed and Fu Bi made Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: now that Yaozuo was openly employed, Yanbo further strengthened his ties—Jie asked that Yanbo be removed and Fu Bi made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 又言諫官吳奎表裏觀望，語甚切直。

translations.literal: He also said that the remonstrance official Wu Kui was watching both ways; and his language was very blunt.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that the remonstrance official Wu Kui was watching both ways; his language was very blunt.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，卻其奏不視，且言將遠竄。

translations.literal: The sovereign was angry, pushed aside the memorial without reading it, and said he would exile Jie far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, pushed aside the memorial without reading it, and said he would exile Jie far away.

sentences.zh: 介徐讀畢，曰：「臣忠憤所激，鼎鑊不避，何辭於謫？」

translations.literal: Jie read it through calmly and said: "I am stirred by loyal indignation—cauldrons and axes I do not avoid; and what words would I have regarding banishment?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie read it through calmly and said: "I am stirred by loyal indignation—cauldrons and axes I do not avoid; what words would I have regarding banishment?"

sentences.zh: 帝急召執政示之曰：「介論事是其職。

translations.literal: The sovereign hurriedly summoned the Chief Councillors and showed them the memorial, saying: "For Jie to discuss affairs is his duty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurriedly summoned the chief ministers and showed them the memorial, saying: "For Jie to discuss affairs is his duty.

sentences.zh: 至謂彥博由妃嬪致宰相，此何言也？

translations.literal: To say that Yanbo became Chief Councillor through imperial consorts—what kind of talk is this?
translations.idiomatic: To say that Yanbo became chief minister through imperial consorts—what kind of talk is this?

sentences.zh: 進用塚司，豈應得預？」

translations.literal: In sum, advancement and employment of the chief steward—how could he have been involved beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: Advancement and employment of the chief steward—how could he have been involved beforehand?"

sentences.zh: 時彥博在前，介責之曰：「彥博宜自省，即有之，不可隱。」

translations.literal: Yanbo was present at the time; and Jie reproached him: "Yanbo ought to examine himself—if it is so, it cannot be hidden."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was present at the time; Jie reproached him: "Yanbo ought to examine himself—if it is so, it cannot be hidden."

sentences.zh: 彥博拜謝不已，帝怒益甚。

translations.literal: Yanbo apologized repeatedly without end; the sovereign's anger grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo apologized repeatedly without end; the emperor's anger grew worse.

sentences.zh: 梁適叱介使下殿，修起居注蔡襄趨進救之。

translations.literal: Liang Shi shouted at Jie to leave the hall; and the reviser of the imperial diary Cai Xiang rushed forward to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shi shouted at Jie to leave the hall; the reviser of the imperial diary Cai Xiang rushed forward to intervene.

sentences.zh: 貶春州別駕，王舉正言以為太重，帝旋悟，明日取其疏入，改置英州，而罷彥博相，吳奎亦出。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant administrator of Chunzhou. Wang Juzheng said the penalty was too heavy; the sovereign soon realized his error. The next day he took in Jie's memorial, changed the posting to Yingzhou, dismissed Yanbo as Chief Councillor, and Wu Kui also left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to assistant administrator of Chunzhou. Wang Juzheng said the penalty was too heavy; the emperor soon realized his error. The next day he took in Jie's memorial, changed the posting to Yingzhou, dismissed Yanbo as chief minister, and Wu Kui also left office.

sentences.zh: 又慮介或道死，有殺直臣名，命中使護之。

translations.literal: The sovereign also feared that Jie might die on the road and they would bear the name of killing a straight official, and ordered palace envoys to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also feared that Jie might die on the road and they would bear the name of killing a straight official, and ordered palace envoys to escort him.

sentences.zh: 梅堯臣、李師中皆賦詩激美，由是直聲動天下，士大夫稱真御史，必曰唐子方而不敢名。

translations.literal: Mei Yaochen and Li Shizhong both wrote poems praising him; and thereby his reputation for integrity shook the realm, and when scholars spoke of a true censor they said Tang Zifang and did not dare use his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Yaochen and Li Shizhong both wrote poems praising him; thereby his reputation for integrity shook the realm, and when scholars spoke of a true censor they said Tang Zifang and did not dare use his personal name.

sentences.zh: 數月，起監郴州稅，通判潭州，知復州，召為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After several months, he was recalled as supervisor of the Chenzhou tax office, vice-prefect of Tanzhou, prefect of Fuzhou, and summoned back as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was recalled as supervisor of the Chenzhou tax office, vice-prefect of Tanzhou, prefect of Fuzhou, and summoned back as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 遣使賜告。

translations.literal: The court sent envoys to grant him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to grant him leave.

sentences.zh: 趣詣闕下。

translations.literal: In sum, he was urged to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was urged to come to court.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝勞之曰：「卯遷謫以來，未嘗以私書至京師，可謂不易所守矣。」

translations.literal: He entered audience; the sovereign comforted him, saying: "Since your banishment you have never sent private letters to the capital—you may truly be called steadfast in what you hold."
translations.idiomatic: He entered audience; the emperor comforted him, saying: "Since your banishment you have never sent private letters to the capital—you may truly be called steadfast in what you hold."

sentences.zh: 介頓首謝，言事益無所顧。

translations.literal: Jie kowtowed in thanks; and in speaking of affairs he was ever more fearless.
translations.idiomatic: Jie kowtowed in thanks; in speaking of affairs he was ever more fearless.

sentences.zh: 他日請曰：「臣既任言責，言之不行將固爭，爭之重以累陛下，願得解職。」

translations.literal: On another day he requested: "Your servant has undertaken the duty of speech; and if my words are not followed I will surely contend further, and heavy contention would burden Your Majesty—I wish to be relieved of the post."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he requested: "Your servant has undertaken the duty of speech; if my words are not followed I will surely contend further, and heavy contention would burden Your Majesty—I wish to be relieved of the post."

sentences.zh: 換工部員外郎、直集賢院，為開封府判官，出知揚州，徙江東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to outer-section member of the Ministry of Works with direct appointment to the Jixian Academy, made judicial officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, sent out as prefect of Yangzhou, moved to transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer-section member of the Ministry of Works with direct appointment to the Jixian Academy, made judicial officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, sent out as prefect of Yangzhou, and moved to transport commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 御史吳中復言，介不宜久居外。

translations.literal: In sum, the censor Wu Zhongfu said that Jie should not long remain outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Wu Zhongfu said that Jie should not long remain outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 文彥博再當國，奏：「介向所言，誠中臣病，願如中復言。」

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo again headed the government and memorialized: "What Jie stated before truly struck at my fault—I wish it done as Zhongfu said."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo again headed the government and memorialized: "What Jie said before truly struck at my fault—I wish it done as Zhongfu said."

sentences.zh: 然但徒河東。

translations.literal: In sum, yet he was only transferred to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was only transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 久之，入為度支副使，進天章閣待制，復知諫院。

translations.literal: After a long interval he entered office as vice commissioner of the fiscal bureau, was advanced to awaiting-edict at the Hanzhang Pavilion, again headed the Remonstrance Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he entered office as vice commissioner of the fiscal bureau, was advanced to awaiting-edict at the Hanzhang Pavilion, and again headed the Remonstrance Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝自至和後，臨朝淵默。

translations.literal: Since the Zhihe era the sovereign at court had been deep and silent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhihe era the emperor at court had been deep and silent.

sentences.zh: 介言：「君臣如天地，以交泰為理。

translations.literal: Jie stated: "Ruler and minister are like heaven and earth—mutual interaction is the principle of order.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "Ruler and minister are like heaven and earth—mutual interaction is the principle of order.

sentences.zh: 願時延群下，發德音，可否萬幾，以幸天下。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would from time to time extend audience to officials below, issue virtuous pronouncements, and approve or reject the myriad affairs of state—to bless the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would from time to time extend audience to officials below, issue virtuous pronouncements, and approve or reject the myriad affairs of state—to bless all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 又論：宮禁幹丐恩澤，出命不由中書，宜有以抑絕；

translations.literal: In sum, he also argued that entreaties for favors from within the palace, with orders issued not through the Secretariat, ought to be blocked;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that entreaties for favors from within the palace, with orders issued not through the Secretariat, ought to be blocked;

sentences.zh: 賜予嬪禦之費，多先朝時十數倍，日加無窮，宜有所朘損；

translations.literal: In sum, gifts and expenses for consorts were often many times greater than under former reigns, increasing daily without end—they ought to be reduced;
translations.idiomatic: gifts and expenses for consorts were often many times greater than under former reigns, increasing daily without end—they ought to be reduced;

sentences.zh: 監司薦舉，多得文法小吏，請令精擇端良敦樸之士，毋使與憸薄者同進；

translations.literal: circuit intendant recommendations often produced petty legal clerks—he asked that upright, sincere, plain men be carefully selected and not allowed to advance together with the sly and shallow;
translations.idiomatic: circuit intendant recommendations often produced petty legal clerks—he asked that upright, sincere, and plain men be carefully selected and not allowed to advance together with the sly and shallow;

sentences.zh: 諸路走馬承受淩擾郡縣，可罷勿遣，以權歸監司；

translations.literal: In sum, mounted couriers on the circuits harassed prefectures and counties—they could be abolished and not sent, returning authority to the intendant;
translations.idiomatic: mounted couriers on the circuits harassed prefectures and counties—they could be abolished and not sent, returning authority to the intendant;

sentences.zh: 兗國公主夜開禁門，宜劾宿衛主吏，以嚴宮省。

translations.literal: In sum, the Princess of Yan opened the forbidden gate at night—the palace guard officers in charge ought to be impeached to tighten palace discipline.
translations.idiomatic: the Princess of Yan opened the forbidden gate at night—the palace guard officers in charge ought to be impeached to tighten palace discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝悉開納之。

translations.literal: The sovereign fully accepted these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fully accepted these proposals.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞韓絳劾宰相富弼，弼家居求罷，絳亦待罪。

translations.literal: The vice censor-in-chief Han Jiang impeached the Chief Councillor Fu Bi; Bi stayed at home and sought dismissal, and Han also awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The vice censor-in-chief Han Jiang impeached the chief minister Fu Bi; Bi stayed at home and sought dismissal, and Han also awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 介與王陶論絳以危法中傷大臣，絳罷。

translations.literal: Jie and Wang Tao argued that Jiang had used dangerous statutes to wound a great minister; and Jiang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Wang Tao argued that Jiang had used dangerous statutes to wound a great minister; Jiang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 介嫌于右宰相，請外，以知荊南。

translations.literal: Ill at ease with the Chief Councillor on the right, Jie requested an outside post and was made prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at ease with the chief minister on the right, Jie requested an outside post and was made prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 敕過門下，知銀台司何郯封還之，留權開封府。

translations.literal: When the edict passed the Secretariat, the director of the Yintai Office He Yan sealed and returned it; and Jie was retained as acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict passed the Secretariat, the director of the Yintai Office He Yan sealed and returned it; Jie was retained as acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 旋以論罷陳升之，亦出知洪州。

translations.literal: In sum, soon, for discussing the dismissal of Chen Shengzhi, he was also sent out as prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for discussing the dismissal of Chen Shengzhi, he was also sent out as prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士、河北都轉運使，樞密直學士、知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles of direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and transport commissioner of Hebei, Privy Council direct academician and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional titles of direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and transport commissioner of Hebei, and Privy Council direct academician and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In sum, in the first year of Zhiping he was summoned as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping he was summoned as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 英宗謂曰：「卿在先朝有直聲，故用卿，非繇左右言也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said to him: "You had a reputation for straight speech in the former reign—therefore I employ you, not because of words from attendants at my side."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong said to him: "You had a reputation for straight speech in the former reign—therefore I employ you, not because of words from attendants at my side."

sentences.zh: 介曰：「臣無狀，陛下過聽，願獻愚忠。

translations.literal: Jie stated: "Your servant is without merit; Your Majesty has over-listened—I wish to offer my foolish loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "Your servant is without merit; Your Majesty has over-listened—I wish to offer my foolish loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自古欲治之主，亦非求絕世驚俗之術，要在順人情而已。

translations.literal: In sum, rulers of old who wished to bring order also did not seek world-shaking techniques—the key lies in complying with human feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of old who wished to bring order also did not seek world-shaking techniques—the key lies in complying with human feelings.

sentences.zh: 祖宗遺德餘烈，在人未遠，願覽已成之業以為監，則天下蒙福矣。

translations.literal: The legacy virtue of the ancestors remains near in people's minds; I wish Your Majesty to view their completed achievement as a mirror—then the realm will receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The legacy virtue of the ancestors remains near in people's minds; I wish Your Majesty to view their completed achievement as a mirror—then all under Heaven will receive blessing.

sentences.zh: 明年，以龍圖閣學士知太原府。

translations.literal: In sum, the next year he was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕視河東，不在中執法下，暫煩卿往耳。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "I regard Hedong as no less important than the central law officers—I temporarily trouble you to go there."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I regard Hedong as no less important than the central law officers—I temporarily trouble you to go there."

sentences.zh: 夏人數擾代州邊，多築堡境上。

translations.literal: In sum, the Western Xia repeatedly harassed the border of Dai Prefecture and often built forts on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia repeatedly harassed the border of Dai Prefecture and often built forts on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 介遣兵悉撤之，移諭以利害，遂不敢動。

translations.literal: Jie sent troops to dismantle them all and sent notice of the benefits and harms involved; and the Xia then did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sent troops to dismantle them all and sent notice of the benefits and harms involved; the Xia then did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，以三司使召。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded to the throne, Jie was summoned as fiscal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong succeeded to the throne, Jie was summoned as fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 熙甯元年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In sum, in the first year of Xining he was appointed participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he was appointed participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 先時，宰相省閱所進文書于待漏舍，同列不得聞。

translations.literal: Previously the Chief Councillors reviewed submitted documents at the vigilance waiting lodge, and their colleagues were not allowed to know their contents.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the chief ministers reviewed submitted documents at the vigilance waiting lodge, and their colleagues were not allowed to know their contents.

sentences.zh: 介謂曾公亮曰：「身在政府而文書弗與知，上或有所問，何辭以對？」

translations.literal: Jie stated to Zeng Gongliang: "Being in the government yet not knowing the documents—if the sovereign should ask something, what words would we have to answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie said to Zeng Gongliang: "Being in the government yet not knowing the documents—if the sovereign should ask something, what words would we have to answer?"

sentences.zh: 乃與同視，後遂為常。

translations.literal: They then viewed them together, afterward this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: They then viewed them together, and afterward this became the custom.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用王安石，公亮因薦之，介言其難大任。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to employ Wang Anshi; Gongliang thereupon recommended him, but Jie stated he was hard to entrust with great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to employ Wang Anshi; Gongliang thereupon recommended him, but Jie said he was hard to entrust with great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「文學不可任耶？

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "May literary learning not be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "May literary learning not be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 吏事不可任耶？

translations.literal: In sum, may administrative affairs not be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: May administrative affairs not be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 經術不可任耶？」

translations.literal: In sum, may classical learning not be entrusted?"
translations.idiomatic: May classical learning not be entrusted?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安石好學而泥古，故論議迂闊，若使為政，必多所變更。」

translations.literal: Jie replied: "Anshi loves learning but is bound to antiquity, so his discussions are far-fetched; if he is allowed to govern he will surely change many things."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Anshi loves learning but is bound to antiquity, so his discussions are far-fetched; if he is allowed to govern he will surely change many things."

sentences.zh: 退謂公亮曰：「安石果用，天下必困擾，諸公當自知之。」

translations.literal: Withdrawing from audience,, he said to Gongliang: "If Anshi is indeed employed, the realm will surely be troubled—you will know that yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawing, he said to Gongliang: "If Anshi is indeed employed, all under Heaven will surely be troubled—you will know that yourselves."

sentences.zh: 中書嘗進除目，數日不決，帝曰：「當問王安石。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat once submitted a list of appointments; for several days there was no decision. The sovereign said: "We should ask Wang Anshi."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat once submitted a list of appointments; for several days there was no decision. The emperor said: "We should ask Wang Anshi."

sentences.zh: 介曰：「陛下以安石可大用，即用之，豈可使中書政事決于翰林學士？

translations.literal: Jie stated: "If Your Majesty thinks Anshi can be greatly used, then use him—how can the government's business of the Secretariat be decided by a Hanlin academician?
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "If Your Majesty thinks Anshi can be greatly used, then use him—how can the government's business of the Secretariat be decided by a Hanlin academician?

sentences.zh: 臣近每聞宣諭某事問安石，可即行之，不可不行，如此則執政何所用，恐非信任大臣之體也。

translations.literal: In sum, i have lately often heard that when edicts instruct that certain matters be asked of Anshi, if he approves they are carried out at once and if he disapproves they are not—if it is thus, of what use are the chief administrators? I fear this is not the proper way to trust great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately often heard that when edicts instruct that certain matters be asked of Anshi, if he approves they are carried out at once and if he disapproves they are not—if it is thus, of what use are the chief administrators? I fear this is not the proper way to trust great ministers.

sentences.zh: 必以臣為不才，願先罷免。」

translations.literal: In sum, if Your Majesty must regard me as without talent, I ask first to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must regard me as without talent, I ask first to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 安石既執政，奏言：「中書處分劄子，皆稱聖旨，不中理者十八九，宜止令中書出牒。」

translations.literal: In sum, after Anshi took charge of the government he memorialized: "The Secretariat's disposition memoranda all say 'imperial intention,' yet nine or eight of ten are unreasonable—it would be better to have only the Secretariat issue formal dispatches."
translations.idiomatic: After Anshi took charge of the government he memorialized: "The Secretariat's disposition memoranda all say 'imperial intention,' yet nine or eight of ten are unreasonable—it would be better to have only the Secretariat issue formal dispatches."

sentences.zh: 帝愕然。

translations.literal: The sovereign was startled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled.

sentences.zh: 介曰：「昔寇准用劄子遷馮拯官不當，拯訴之，太宗謂：'前代中書用堂牒，乃權臣假此為威福。

translations.literal: Jie stated: "Formerly Kou Zhun used a memorandum to transfer Feng Zheng to a post improperly; Zheng appealed. Taizong said: 'In former dynasties the Secretariat used hall posts—powerful ministers used this to wield prestige and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "Formerly Kou Zhun used a memorandum to transfer Feng Zheng to a post improperly; Zheng appealed. Taizong said: 'In former dynasties the Secretariat used hall posts—powerful ministers used this to wield prestige and favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖時以堂帖重於敕命，遂削去之。

translations.literal: In sum, in Taizu's time hall notes weighed more heavily than edict commands, so they were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's time hall notes weighed more heavily than edict commands, so they were cut off.

sentences.zh: 今復用劄子，何異堂帖？

translations.literal: In sum, to use memoranda again now—how is it different from hall posts?
translations.idiomatic: To use memoranda again now—how is it different from hall posts?

sentences.zh: '張洎因言：'廢劄子，則中書行事，別無公式。」

translations.literal: In sum, zhang Zhi then said: 'If memoranda are abolished, the Secretariat has no other formula for conducting business.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi then said: 'If memoranda are abolished, the Secretariat has no other formula for conducting business.'

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：'大事則降敕，其當用紮子，亦須奏裁。

translations.literal: Taizong said: 'For great affairs issue an edict; and when memoranda should be used, they too must be memorialized for decision.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: 'For great affairs issue an edict; when memoranda should be used, they too must be memorialized for decision.'

sentences.zh: '此所以稱聖旨也。

translations.literal: In sum, that is why they say 'imperial intention.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why they say 'imperial intention.'

sentences.zh: 如安石言，則是政不自天子出，使輔臣皆忠賢，猶為擅命，苟非其人，豈不害國？」

translations.literal: As Anshi proposes, government would not proceed from the Son of Heaven; and even if the assisting ministers were all loyal and worthy it would still be usurping command, and if they were not such men would it not harm the state?"
translations.idiomatic: As Anshi proposes, government would not proceed from the Son of Heaven; even if the assisting ministers were all loyal and worthy it would still be usurping command, and if they were not such men would it not harm the state?"

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign thought this right and stopped the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this right and stopped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 介自是數與安石爭論。

translations.literal: In sum, from then on Jie repeatedly debated with Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jie repeatedly debated with Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石強辯，而帝主其說。

translations.literal: Anshi argued forcefully, and the sovereign sided with his views.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi argued forcefully, and the emperor sided with his views.

sentences.zh: 介不勝憤，疽發於背，薨，年六十。

translations.literal: Jie could not overcome his anger; and a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Jie could not overcome his anger; a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 介為人簡伉，以敢言見憚。

translations.literal: In sum, jie as a man was simple and upright and was feared for his willingness to speak bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: Jie as a man was simple and upright and was feared for his willingness to speak bluntly.

sentences.zh: 每言官缺，眾皆望介處之，觀其風采。

translations.literal: In sum, whenever a censor's post fell vacant, everyone looked to Jie to fill it and watched his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a censor's post fell vacant, everyone looked to Jie to fill it and watched his bearing.

sentences.zh: 神宗謂其先朝遺直，故大用之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong regarded him as a straight legacy of the former reign and therefore employed him on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong regarded him as a straight legacy of the former reign and therefore employed him on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 然居政府，遭時有為，而扼于安石，少所建明，聲名減於諫官、御史時。

translations.literal: In sum, yet while in the government he encountered an activist age and was constrained by Anshi, so he established little—his renown was less than in his days as remonstrance official and censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while in the government he encountered an activist age and was constrained by Anshi, so he established little—his renown was less than in his days as remonstrance official and censor.

sentences.zh: 比疾亟，帝臨問流涕，復幸其第吊哭，以畫像不類，命取禁中舊藏本賜其家。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical the sovereign visited him in person and wept; he again favored Jie's residence to mourn and weep. Because the portrait was unlike him, he ordered the old copy kept in the forbidden storehouse to be taken out and bestowed on the family.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical the emperor visited him in person and wept; he again favored Jie's residence to mourn and weep. Because the portrait was unlike him, he ordered the old copy kept in the forbidden storehouse to be taken out and bestowed on the family.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡曰質肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites; and his posthumous name was Zhisu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites; his posthumous name was Zhisu.

sentences.zh: 子淑問、義問，孫恕。

translations.literal: His sons were Shuwen and Yiwen; and his grandson was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shuwen and Yiwen; his grandson was Shu.

sentences.zh: 子 淑問

translations.literal: In sum, son: Shuwen
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shuwen

sentences.zh: 淑問字士憲。

translations.literal: In brief, shuwen's courtesy name was Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen's courtesy name was Shixian.

sentences.zh: 第進士，至殿中丞。

translations.literal: In brief, he passed the examinations and rose to palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations and rose to palace aide.

sentences.zh: 神宗以其家世，擢監察御史裏行，諭以謹家法、務大體。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong, because of his family's standing, promoted him to supernumerary investigating censor and instructed him to keep strict household discipline and attend to the larger pattern of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong, because of his family's standing, promoted him to supernumerary investigating censor and instructed him to keep strict household discipline and attend to the larger pattern of affairs.

sentences.zh: 淑問見帝初即位，銳於治，因言：「中旨數下，一出特斷，當謹出納、別枉直，使命令必行。

translations.literal: In brief, shuwen saw that the emperor had just succeeded and was keen on governance, and said: "Central edicts issue frequently, each a special decision—we ought carefully to control what goes out, distinguish crooked from straight, and ensure that orders are surely carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen saw that the emperor had just succeeded and was keen on governance, and said: "Central edicts issue frequently, each a special decision—we ought carefully to control what goes out, distinguish crooked from straight, and ensure that orders are surely carried out.

sentences.zh: 今詔書求直言，而久無所施用，必欲屈群策以起治道，願行其言。」

translations.literal: Now edicts seek blunt counsel, yet for long nothing has been applied—we must wish to bend the multitude of strategies to raise the way of order; and I ask that the words be put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: Now edicts seek blunt counsel, yet for long nothing has been applied—we must wish to bend the multitude of strategies to raise the way of order; I ask that the words be put into practice."

sentences.zh: 初，詔侍臣講讀。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict had ordered attendant ministers to lecture and study.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an edict had ordered attendant ministers to lecture and study.

sentences.zh: 淑問言：「王者之學，不必分章句、飾文辭。

translations.literal: Shuwen stated: "The learning of a king need not divide into chapter and sentence or adorn literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen said: "The learning of a king need not divide into chapter and sentence or adorn literary phrasing.

sentences.zh: 稽古聖人治天下之道，歷代致興亡之由，延登正人，博訪世務，以求合先王，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Examine antiquity for the way the sages governed all under Heaven, the causes of rise and fall in successive ages; and extend audience to upright men and broadly inquire into worldly affairs to seek conformity with the former kings—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: Examine antiquity for the way the sages governed all under Heaven, the causes of rise and fall in successive ages; extend audience to upright men and broadly inquire into worldly affairs to seek conformity with the former kings—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 河北饑，流人就食京師，官振廩給食，來者不止。

translations.literal: At the time when Hebei suffered famine, refugees came to the capital to find food; the government opened granaries and gave grain, yet arrivals did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei suffered famine, refugees came to the capital to find food; the government opened granaries and gave grain, yet arrivals did not cease.

sentences.zh: 淑問曰：「出粟不繼，是誘之失業而就死地也。」

translations.literal: Shuwen stated: "Issuing grain without continuing supply is to lure people to lose their livelihood and go to their deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen said: "Issuing grain without continuing supply is to lure people to lose their livelihood and go to their deaths."

sentences.zh: 條三策上之。

translations.literal: In brief, he set forth three policies and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth three policies and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 滕甫為中丞，淑問力數其短，帝以為邀名，乃詔避其父三司使，出通判復州。

translations.literal: At the time when Teng Fu was vice censor-in-chief, Shuwen repeatedly pressed his shortcomings; the emperor thought he was seeking a name and ordered him to avoid his father the fiscal commissioner—he was sent out as vice-prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng Fu was vice censor-in-chief, Shuwen repeatedly pressed his shortcomings; the emperor thought he was seeking a name and ordered him to avoid his father the fiscal commissioner—he was sent out as vice-prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，知真州，提點湖北刑獄，言新法不便，乞解使事，黜知信陽軍，以病免。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made prefect of Zhenzhou and intendant of Hubei judicial affairs; and he said the new laws were inconvenient, begged to be relieved of intendant duties, was demoted to military prefect of Xinyang, and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was made prefect of Zhenzhou and intendant of Hubei judicial affairs; he said the new laws were inconvenient, begged to be relieved of intendant duties, was demoted to military prefect of Xinyang, and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 數年，起知宣州，徙湖州，入為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: After several years, he was recalled as prefect of Xuanzhou, moved to Huzhou, and entered office as outer-section member of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled as prefect of Xuanzhou, moved to Huzhou, and entered office as outer-section member of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又引疾求外，帝以為避事，降監撫州酒稅。

translations.literal: He again cited illness and sought an outside post; and the emperor regarded it as shirking duty and demoted him to supervisor of the Fuzhou wine tax.
translations.idiomatic: He again cited illness and sought an outside post; the emperor regarded it as shirking duty and demoted him to supervisor of the Fuzhou wine tax.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，司馬光薦其行己有恥，難進，召為左司諫，以病致仕，數月卒。

translations.literal: At the time when Zhezong succeeded, Sima Guang recommended that his conduct showed a sense of shame and that he was hard to advance; he was summoned as left remonstrance official, resigned on illness, and died several months later.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong succeeded, Sima Guang recommended that his conduct showed a sense of shame and that he was hard to advance; he was summoned as left remonstrance official, resigned on illness, and died several months later.

sentences.zh: 子 義問

translations.literal: His son: Yiwen
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yiwen

sentences.zh: 義問字士宣。

translations.literal: In brief, yiwen's courtesy name was Shixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwen's courtesy name was Shixuan.

sentences.zh: 善文辭，鎖廳試禮部，用舉者召試秘閣，父介引嫌罷之。

translations.literal: Skilled in literary composition, he took the locked-hall examination in the Ministry of Rites; and because of a recommender he was summoned to trial at the Secretariat Pavilion, but his father Jie cited conflict of interest and the summons was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in literary composition, he took the locked-hall examination in the Ministry of Rites; because of a recommender he was summoned to trial at the Secretariat Pavilion, but his father Jie cited conflict of interest and the summons was canceled.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，辟京西轉運司管勾文字。

translations.literal: In brief, during the Xining era he was recruited to the Jingxi transport commission as clerk for documents.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he was recruited to the Jingxi transport commission as clerk for documents.

sentences.zh: 神宗覽本道章奏，知義問所為。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reviewed memorials from that circuit and learned what Yiwen had done.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong reviewed memorials from that circuit and learned what Yiwen had done.

sentences.zh: 以其名訪輔臣，因黃好謙領使事，諭之曰：「唐義問風力強敏，行且用矣，可面詔之。」

translations.literal: He inquired about him among assisting ministers; and because Huang Haoqian headed the commission, he instructed him: "Tang Yiwen is forceful and keen—he will soon be employed; and you may inform him face to face by edict."
translations.idiomatic: He inquired about him among assisting ministers; because Huang Haoqian headed the commission, he instructed him: "Tang Yiwen is forceful and keen—he will soon be employed; you may inform him face to face by edict."

sentences.zh: 尋以為司農管當公事。

translations.literal: In brief, soon he was made clerk in charge of affairs in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made clerk in charge of affairs in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 方行手實法，所在騷然。

translations.literal: In brief, just as the household registration law was being implemented, everywhere was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the household registration law was being implemented, everywhere was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 義問言：「今造簿甫二歲，民不堪命，不宜復改為。」

translations.literal: Yiwen stated: "Registers have been compiled for only two years and the people cannot bear the burden—it is not fitting to change them again."
translations.idiomatic: Yiwen said: "Registers have been compiled for only two years and the people cannot bear the burden—it is not fitting to change them again."

sentences.zh: 從曾孝寬使河東，還奏事，記利害綱目於笏，帝取而熟視之，曆舉以問，應析如流。

translations.literal: He followed Zeng Xiaokuan on mission to Hedong; returning to report, he noted points of benefit and harm on his tablet. The sovereign took it and studied it closely, going through each item and asking—he answered as if unraveling threads.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zeng Xiaokuan on mission to Hedong; returning to report, he noted points of benefit and harm on his tablet. The emperor took it and studied it closely, going through each item and asking—he answered as if unraveling threads.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「欲見卿，非今日也。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said with pleasure: "I wished to see you—not only today."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure: "I wished to see you—not only today."

sentences.zh: 擢湖南轉運判官。

translations.literal: In brief, he was promoted to vice transport commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice transport commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 一路敷免役錢，又分戶五等，儲其羨為別賦，號「家力錢」，義問奏除之。

translations.literal: On that circuit exemption from corvée money was spread broadly, and households were divided into five grades to store the surplus as a separate levy called "household strength money"; and Yiwen memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: On that circuit exemption from corvée money was spread broadly, and households were divided into five grades to store the surplus as a separate levy called "household strength money"; Yiwen memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 移使京西，文彥博守西都，義問求罷去。

translations.literal: In brief, transferred as commissioner of Jingxi, when Wen Yanbo guarded the western capital Yiwen sought to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred as commissioner of Jingxi, when Wen Yanbo guarded the western capital Yiwen sought to resign.

sentences.zh: 彥博告以再入相時，嘗薦其父，晚同為執政，相得甚歡，故義問乃止。

translations.literal: In brief, yanbo told him that when he entered the chief ministership again he had once recommended Yiwen's father, and in later years they served together in government and got on very well—so Yiwen stopped his request.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo told him that when he entered the chief ministership again he had once recommended Yiwen's father, and in later years they served together in government and got on very well—so Yiwen stopped his request.

sentences.zh: 時陝西大舉兵，多亡卒，所至成聚。

translations.literal: At the time a great campaign was launched in Shaanxi and many soldiers deserted; and wherever they went they gathered in bands.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a great campaign was launched in Shaanxi and many soldiers deserted; wherever they went they gathered in bands.

sentences.zh: 義問請令詣官自陳，給券續食，人以為便。

translations.literal: In brief, yiwen asked that they be allowed to present themselves at government offices, be given certificates and continued rations—people regarded it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwen asked that they be allowed to present themselves at government offices, be given certificates and continued rations—people regarded it as convenient.

sentences.zh: 會有不悅之者，免歸。

translations.literal: At the time when someone who disliked him came to power, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When someone who disliked him came to power, he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，起知齊州，提點京東刑獄、河北轉運副使。

translations.literal: In brief, in the Yuanyou era he was recalled as prefect of Qizhou, intendant of Jingdong judicial affairs, and vice transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era he was recalled as prefect of Qizhou, intendant of Jingdong judicial affairs, and vice transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 屬邑尉因捕盜誤遺火，盜逸去，民家被焚，訟尉故縱火。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county a constable while pursuing bandits accidentally caused a fire; and the bandits escaped and a commoner's house was burned—the people sued the constable for deliberately setting the fire.
translations.idiomatic: In a subordinate county a constable while pursuing bandits accidentally caused a fire; the bandits escaped and a commoner's house was burned—the people sued the constable for deliberately setting the fire.

sentences.zh: 郡守執尉，抑使服，義問辨出之，方旱而雨。

translations.literal: The prefect arrested the constable and pressured him to confess; and Yiwen argued and secured his release—just then there was drought and it rained.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect arrested the constable and pressured him to confess; Yiwen argued and secured his release—just then there was drought and it rained.

sentences.zh: 用彥博薦，加集賢修撰，帥荊南，請廢渠陽諸砦。

translations.literal: On Yanbo's recommendation he was given the additional title of compiler of the Jixian Academy and commanded Jingnan; and he asked to abolish the forts at Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: On Yanbo's recommendation he was given the additional title of compiler of the Jixian Academy and commanded Jingnan; he asked to abolish the forts at Quyang.

sentences.zh: 蠻楊晟秀斷之以叛，即拜湖北轉運使，討降之，復砦為州。

translations.literal: The Man chieftain Yang Shengxiu severed relations and rebelled; and Yiwen was at once made transport commissioner of Hubei, campaigned and received their surrender, and restored the forts as prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Yang Shengxiu severed relations and rebelled; Yiwen was at once made transport commissioner of Hubei, campaigned and received their surrender, and restored the forts as prefectures.

sentences.zh: 進直龍圖閣，以集賢殿修撰知廣州。

translations.literal: In brief, he was advanced to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and made Jixian Hall compiler and prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and made Jixian Hall compiler and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 章惇秉政，治棄渠陽罪，貶舒州團練副使。

translations.literal: At the time when Zhang Dun held power he was punished for abandoning Quyang and was demoted to military vice-commissioner of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun held power he was punished for abandoning Quyang and was demoted to military vice-commissioner of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後七年，復故官，知潁昌府，卒。

translations.literal: Seven years later his former rank was restored and he was made prefect of Yingchang; and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later his former rank was restored and he was made prefect of Yingchang; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫 恕

translations.literal: His grandson: Shu
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shu

sentences.zh: 恕，崇甯初，為華陽令，以不能奉行茶法，忤使者，謝病免歸。

translations.literal: Shu, in the early Chongning era, was magistrate of Huayang; and because he could not enforce the tea law he offended the commissioner, resigned on illness, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, in the early Chongning era, was magistrate of Huayang; because he could not enforce the tea law he offended the commissioner, resigned on illness, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 其弟意方為南陵令，亦以病自免，兄弟杜門躬耕。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi was magistrate of Nanling and also resigned on illness; and the brothers shut their doors and plowed for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi was magistrate of Nanling and also resigned on illness; the brothers shut their doors and plowed for themselves.

sentences.zh: 恕尋以宣教郎致仕。

translations.literal: In brief, shu soon retired as Instructor in the Promotion of Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shu soon retired as Instructor in the Promotion of Virtue.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，御史中丞許翰言其高行，詔起為監察御史。

translations.literal: In brief, in the first year of Jingkang the vice censor-in-chief Xu Han spoke of his lofty conduct and an edict recalled him as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang the vice censor-in-chief Xu Han spoke of his lofty conduct and an edict recalled him as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 意亦以宰相吳敏薦，召對，而貧不能行，竟餓死江陵山中。

translations.literal: In brief, yi was also recommended by the chief minister Wu Min and summoned to audience, but being poor he could not travel and ultimately starved to death in the mountains of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was also recommended by the chief minister Wu Min and summoned to audience, but being poor he could not travel and ultimately starved to death in the mountains of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 論曰：拯為開封，其政嚴明，人到於今稱之。

translations.literal: The evaluators say: As prefect of Kaifeng, Bao's government was strict and clear, and people to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: As prefect of Kaifeng, Bao's government was strict and clear, and people to this day praise him.

sentences.zh: 而不尚苛刻，推本忠厚，非孔子所謂剛者乎：奎博學清重，君子人也。

translations.literal: Yet he did not esteem harshness; and tracing his roots he was fundamentally generous and loyal—is this not what Confucius called being firm? Kui was broadly learned, pure and weighty—a man of the noble sort.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not esteem harshness; tracing his roots he was fundamentally generous and loyal—is this not what Confucius called being firm? Kui was broadly learned, pure and weighty—a man of the noble sort.

sentences.zh: 抃所至善治，民思不忘，猶古遺愛。

translations.literal: What Bian attained was excellent governance; and the people remember him and do not forget—like ancient lingering affection.
translations.idiomatic: What Bian attained was excellent governance; the people remember him and do not forget—like ancient lingering affection.

sentences.zh: 介敢言，聲動天下，斯古遺直也。

translations.literal: In brief, jie dared to speak and his voice shook the realm—he is the straight legacy of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Jie dared to speak and his voice shook the realm—he is the straight legacy of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 夫聽諫者，明君所難，以唐文皇猶弗終於魏徵，觀四臣面諍，鯁吭逆心，或不能堪，而仁宗容之無咈，誠盛德之主哉！

translations.literal: To heed remonstrance is what a clear ruler finds difficult; and even Tang Taizong did not carry through with Wei Zheng to the end. Watching these four ministers remonstrate to their faces, their throats blocked and words against the heart—some could not bear it—yet Renzong accommodated them without offense: truly a sovereign of magnificent virtue!
translations.idiomatic: To heed remonstrance is what a clear ruler finds difficult; even Tang Taizong did not carry through with Wei Zheng to the end. Watching these four ministers remonstrate to their faces, their throats blocked and words against the heart—some could not bear it—yet Renzong accommodated them without offense: truly a sovereign of magnificent virtue!

sentences.zh: 屼世孝，淑問難進，義問強敏，恕高行不隕家聲，有足美雲。

translations.literal: Upholding filial virtue from generation to generation: Shuwen was hard to advance, Yiwen forceful and keen, and Shu's lofty conduct did not dim the family's reputation—there is ample praise in this.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding filial virtue from generation to generation: Shuwen was hard to advance, Yiwen forceful and keen, and Shu's lofty conduct did not dim the family's reputation—there is ample praise in this.
